raw.title: EMEA Counsel
raw.description:
About Clay

AI is unleashing the biggest wave of company creation in history. Clay's mission is to be the engine those companies use to grow to their full potential.

Clay predicts the next best action for your business and then helps you take it. We started by aggregating the best data for B2B companies. Then, we built the infrastructure to run any personalized campaign on top of it, including emails, ads, landing pages, and workflows that make reps more productive. Now, we're building agents that can help grow your company for you. We're already helping thousands of customers — including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Visa — go to market with unique data, signals, and AI research.

In 2026, we raised a $115M Series D at $7.1B Valuation led by Wellington — and are on track to cross $200M in revenue this quarter. We also launched a $1M Scholarship fund for GTME Education.

Some things to know about us:

  • Our community includes 17,000+ customers, 200+ integration partners, 125+ agencies, 50+ Clay clubs, and 30k members on Slack.

  • Our culture is unique inside and outside of work. Our team members are also DJs, activists, writers, clowns, marathoners, skydivers, psychedelic therapists, social workers, and more.

  • All employees can work with world-class coaches who specialize in creativity, management, and more.

  • Our operating principles — including negative maintenance and non-attached action — guide our work. Read more about them here.

  • Read about us in the NYT, Forbes, First Round Review, and more.

Hear from our employees directly on our Glassdoor page!

EMEA Counsel

Clay is seeking an EMEA Counsel as our first dedicated legal team member in the region. You will help Clay scale internationally by providing practical, business-oriented support across privacy, product, commercial, regulatory, and go-to-market matters throughout the UK and Europe.

In this broad role, you will work at the intersection of technology, data, and rapidly evolving regulation. You will partner closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Security, People, and Partnerships, as well as Clay’s U.S.-based Legal team.

You will advise on European privacy and technology regulations–including GDPR, ePrivacy, direct-marketing rules, and the EU AI Act -- providing in-time-zone legal support for our growing EMEA business and helping establish scalable international legal processes.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as the primary legal partner for Clay’s EMEA teams during European business hours.

  • Advise on EU, UK, and Middle East privacy and data protection requirements (GDPR, UK GDPR, data subject rights, international transfers, and privacy-by-design).

  • Partner with Clay’s Privacy, Product & AI counsel on European data, product, and AI regulatory matters.

  • Monitor regional technology and privacy regulations, translating legal developments into clear product requirements, policies, and guidance.

  • Support the EMEA go-to-market team by negotiating sales agreements, DPAs, customer terms, and strategic partnerships.

  • Address complex customer inquiries regarding privacy, data governance, security, and AI practices during enterprise sales cycles.

  • Guide expansion into new European jurisdictions, coordinating local counsel where necessary.

  • Collaborate with People and external counsel on local employment, entity setup, and corporate structuring.

  • Build scalable legal infrastructure, including contract templates, playbooks, and self-service processes.

What You'll Bring

  • Qualified lawyer in the UK or an EU jurisdiction (or equivalent qualification).

  • 8+ years of legal experience, preferably 4+ years in-house at a fast-growing B2B technology company.

  • Strong working knowledge of GDPR, European privacy, data protection, and marketing regulations.

  • Familiarity with the EU AI Act and the broader European AI regulatory framework.

  • Proven track record negotiating complex B2B SaaS agreements, DPAs, and enterprise contracts.

  • Ability to thrive as a generalist in a fast-paced environment and build practical legal frameworks from first principles.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills across technical, executive, and commercial audiences.

  • Experience with data-intensive platforms, AI, or sales technology.

  • Experience supporting U.S. tech companies expanding into EMEA

Preferred Qualifications

  • CIPP/E and/or AIGP certifications

raw.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Machine Learning
raw.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why the Cohere TPM role?

As our Generative Machine Learning organization has continued growing, we are looking for more Technical Program Managers to join the team!

At Cohere, TPMs are pivotal to our success, being seen as operational experts specializing in cross-functional efforts. Great TPMs at Cohere are well-rounded, executing with precision at the tactical level, while partnering with senior leaders and shaping the big picture at a strategic level, and the opportunities are endless in growing the scale and impact of their work. Cohere’s TPMs would often be described as organized, execution-oriented, pragmatic leaders who are adaptable to the needs of the company and the programs they lead.

As a reward for the depth and breadth of expertize that you bring to the table, you will get to work alongside some of the most talented AI researchers and industry experts in the world on building cutting edge AI technology. No day will be the same as the one before, and the dynamic high growth environment will be absolutely perfect for anyone excited about solving novel problems, bringing structure to oftentimes chaotic and fast-paced environments, and ambitious about scaling their own impact and growth alongside the company!

Please note: While we are remote-first and accept candidates from all over the world, we are highly prioritizing hiring for people who are within 1-2 hours of British Standard Time (BST).

As a Machine Learning Technical Program Manager, you will:

  • Establish, improve, and scale foundational processes that allow the Generative Modeling teams to execute better, faster, and more predictably

  • Scale the operational capacity and effectiveness of the Modeling TPM team in collaboration with the Modeling TPM lead to ensure the function can remain lean and effective during a period of the program portfolio complexity and size continuing to rapidly increase

  • Flexibly adapt to the needs of the company, programs, and the team from tackling long-horizon programs that can span quarters or even years to jumping onto often highly ambiguous short-term challenges that can have company-wide impact

  • Partner directly with leaders within and outside of the Modeling organization on efforts to design, train and improve our core generative models

  • Lead cross-functional, oftentimes company-wide programs and strategic initiatives, collaborating and coordinating with cross-functional teams such as Product, Engineering, Legal, Platform, Infra, Policy, and Finance

  • Operate as an organizational expert in improving engineering execution rigor and operations on the ground, while contributing to the strategic layer in areas such as long-term strategic planning with senior modeling leadership

  • Map out dependencies and risks, and ensure that cross-functional execution across the program runs smoothly, communicating status with non-technical and technical stakeholders and senior management

  • Both own and enable a useful communication flow of priorities, ideas, and knowledge throughout and beyond the Modeling organization in line with your programs

  • Respond quickly to program-level changes, clarifying new scope, and managing resource needs in response to evolving priorities

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • 5-10 years as a Technical Program Manager AND 5+ years of experience working directly on AI/ML. Strong preference for candidates that have worked directly in building foundation models.

  • In-depth knowledge of machine learning, particularly when it comes to Natural Language Processing & Large Language Models (LLMs). Bonus points for experience with Multimodal AI.

  • Experience with working in a chaotic, fast paced, low structure environment. We need someone who is pragmatic, can roll up their sleeves when needed, and can function at the tactical and strategic level to do whatever it takes to make Cohere’s models succeed

  • Personal hands-on understanding of the unique challenges of managing projects and programs in the AI/ML development space as opposed to traditional software program management

  • Managed projects & programs requiring a strong general business acumen, such as coordinating with Finance on reporting needs or Policy on regulatory compliance matters — the broader your experience beyond ML technical program management, the better!

  • (optional, but preferred) Have technical experience in a hands-on capacity. We don’t necessarily need someone with hands on experience training models, but you need to feel comfortable sitting in the same rooms with some of the best researchers in the world, working on highly complex, cutting edge ML problems

If some of the above - other than the ML TPM experience - doesn’t line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply! If you consider yourself a thoughtful worker, a lifelong learner, and a kind and playful team member, Cohere is the place for you.

We welcome applicants of all kinds and are committed to providing both an equal opportunity process and work environment. We value and celebrate diversity and strive to create an inclusive work environment for all.

Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks:

  • A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

  • Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

  • RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

  • 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

  • Annual enrichment benefits:

    Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

    Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

  • 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

  • Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How and Where We Work:

  • Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

  • For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

  • For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

  • Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an ----- or ----- email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

raw.description:
About Us

Condukt is the next-generation compliance platform for financial services, offering an agentic solution powered by real-time data for business identity.

Always-on and policy-aware, Condukt enables financial institutions and fintechs to gain actionable insights into business verification - unlocking growth, increasing efficiency, and strengthening compliance.

We were founded by former operators and builders with deep experience in banking, payments, and lending. Today, our team spans across London and Porto, bringing together engineers, product owners, and operators from companies like Revolut, Meta, Block (Square), SumUp, American Express, Yandex, and OakNorth.

Trusted by leading regulated entities, including Wise, Tide, Mollie, Shift4, Flatpay, and myPOS, Condukt is backed by top investors, including Lightspeed Venture Partners and MMC Ventures.

 

Position Overview

As a GTM Associate, you’ll sit at the centre of Condukt’s commercial engine, generating new pipeline across financial services and working hand in hand with our Account Executives to turn it into revenue.

You’ll build opportunities from the ground up: reaching high-growth fintechs and financial institutions with well-researched outreach, qualifying inbound interest quickly, and running first discovery conversations. Your work doesn’t end at the first meeting. You’ll stay on the deal with our Account Executives, help build the customer relationship and, as you grow, lead smaller deals end to end alongside an AE.

As an early-stage, fast-growing company, we value people who take ownership, move with urgency, and are excited to help build both a market-leading product and a repeatable enterprise sales motion. You’ll work closely with our AI Deployment Strategists, Product, Engineering, and Leadership to shape how we sell, who we sell to, and how we win.

If you’re at the start of your commercial career, energised by meeting new people, and keen to take on more responsibility fast, this role is for you.

 

What you’ll do:

  • Own early-stage pipeline creation with fintechs and financial institutions that match our ideal customer profile

  • Research and map target accounts, identifying the right C-level Risk & Compliance, Operations, and Product leaders to engage

  • Help build and run our outbound motion, with sharp, well-researched messaging across email, LinkedIn, phone and events. Test creative formats beyond the usual sequences, and turn what works into a repeatable playbook

  • Respond fast to inbound interest and qualify every lead on fit, urgency and decision-makers

  • Lead discovery calls, support AEs on live deals and, as you grow, lead smaller deals end to end

  • Bring what you hear from the market back to Product and Leadership, helping shape who we sell to and spot new market opportunities

  • Pick up whatever the business needs next: priorities will shift as we scale, and you’ll help shape where we go

What you bring:

  • 1-3 years in a client-facing or target-carrying role, with a proven record of booking net-new meetings

  • Genuine energy for meeting people, and the confidence to pick up the phone, walk into a room of strangers and start the conversation

  • Resilience in the face of rejection, and the drive to keep going for the wins

  • Ability to learn fast, handle ambiguity and change course when priorities shift

  • Hands-on attitude, with a focus on outcomes rather than titles

  • Intellectual curiosity about the compliance space

  • Fluency with AI and data tools to work faster and smarter

  • Strong organisation across follow-ups, sequences and your CRM

  • Low-ego, collaborative approach and openness to feedback

  • Genuine interest in fintech and how financial institutions onboard customers and manage risk

  • Excellent written and spoken English

  • The right to work in the UK

Bonus:

  • Sales experience preferred, but not required for the role

  • Background in fintech, banking, payments, or lending ecosystems

  • Second language proficiency (German, French, and Dutch, especially valued)

 

Our offer:

  • Tackle meaningful problems with real-world impact

  • Competitive salary and equity package

  • Flat hierarchy with direct access to the founders

  • Hybrid, 3 days a week in our London office

  • Top-of-the-line equipment

  • Private health insurance, plus sick and compassionate leave as needed

raw.title: Senior Analyst - Commodities Trade Support
raw.description:
We are seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Senior Analyst to join the Commodities Trade Support team. The successful candidate will provide end-to-end operational support across the commodities trading lifecycle, ensuring accurate trade capture, timely issue resolution, risk mitigation, and strong stakeholder engagement with Front Office, Risk, Finance, Treasury, Technology, and external counterparties.

The role covers physical and financial commodity products across Energy, Metals, Agricultural Products, and Environmental Markets, supporting both exchange-traded and OTC transactions.

The individual will act as a key escalation point for complex trade issues while driving process improvements and operational excellence.


Key Responsibilities

  • Validate and manage trade capture for commodity transactions across multiple asset classes, ensuring accurate booking and representation across trading and risk platforms.

  • Own front-to-back trade support activities during the T0/T+1 window, partnering with Trading, Risk, and Operations teams to ensure trades are verified, reconciled, and operationally ready for offshore handover.

  • Investigate and resolve trade breaks, discrepancies, and operational exceptions within agreed SLAs, performing root cause analysis where required.

  • Maintain trade static data, pricing parameters, and settlement instructions to support accurate downstream processing.

  • Support physical and financial commodity products, including Crude Oil and Refined Products, Natural Gas and LNG, Power and Renewables, Metals and Mining Products, Agricultural Commodities, and Carbon and Environmental Products.

  • Monitor commodity-specific lifecycle events, including nominations, allocations, deliveries, inventory movements, and settlement activities where applicable.

  • Coordinate with logistics, scheduling, commercial teams, exchanges, brokers, and counterparties to facilitate the smooth processing of physical and financial transactions.

  • Act as a key point of contact for Traders, Structurers, Risk Managers, Finance, and external counterparties, ensuring timely resolution of operational and trade-related issues.

  • Ensure adherence to internal control frameworks, audit requirements, and operational risk standards, participating in incident management and escalation processes as required.

  • Identify and deliver process improvements, automation opportunities, and control enhancements to increase operational efficiency.

  • Contribute to strategic change initiatives, system implementations, platform migrations, and operating model improvements.

Essential

  • Experience within Commodities Trade Support, Commodities Middle Office, Trade Operations, Energy Operations, or Product Control / Operations Support.

  • Experience supporting commodity trading businesses, merchants, or investment banks.

  • Strong understanding of the trade lifecycle for OTC and exchange-traded commodity products.

  • Experience managing trade capture, reconciliations, settlements, and exception management.

  • Proven ability to interact directly with trading desks and senior stakeholders.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

How We Work:

Delta Capita is an equal opportunity employer. We positively encourage applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of age, colour, disability, national origin, ancestry, race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. If you require any reasonable adjustments through your interview process, please use the designated space within the application questionnaire.

This is a permanent full-time position located in London with hybrid working. As the selection and interview process is ongoing, please submit your application in English as soon as possible. If your profile is selected, a member of our team will contact you within 4 weeks. A valid UK working permit is mandatory for this role.

Expectations regarding hybrid working: 

As we are a Service Provider and Consulting firm servicing clients, our policy for physically working from the office (which may be the clients' offices or our own offices depending on the client) aligns to what our clients' policies and expectations are and these vary. Most of our clients now require a minimum of 3 days per week in the office, 2 days from home, and accordingly this is also the minimum expectation that Delta Capita require. However, some of our clients have now moved up to 4 days and even 5 days in the office and we require candidates to be flexible to meet our client demands.

Who We Are:

Delta Capita Group is a global managed services, consulting, and solutions provider with a unique combination of experience in Financial Services and technology innovation capability. Our mission is to reinvent the financial services value chain providing technology-based mutualised services for financial institutions for non-differentiating services.

Our 3 offerings are:

  • Managed Services

  • Consulting & Solutions

  • Technology

 

To know more about Delta Capita and our culture click here: Working at DC – Delta Capita

About the Company
 
e.l.f. Beauty's purpose is to make the world a better place for every eye, lip, and face.

Position Summary

The Associate Director, Transportation for the UK & EU is accountable for the performance, cost, and future-readiness of our regional transportation network. This role owns the day-to-day service levels our retail partners and consumers expect, while continuously reviewing and challenging the cost base, and — critically — developing the strategy that ensures our 3PL and carrier capacity can absorb the rapid growth ahead.

Sitting in London and reporting to the US-based Associate Director of Transportation, you will be the regional leader who bridges global strategy with local execution. You will partner closely with our 3PL providers, internal commercial and supply chain teams, and the US transportation function to deliver a network that is reliable, cost-efficient, scalable, and aligned to e.l.f.'s values.

Responsibilities:

Service Level Management

· Own end-to-end transportation service performance across the UK and EU, including on-time delivery, order fulfillment accuracy, and transit-time reliability for retail, wholesale, and e-commerce channels.

· Define, track, and publish transportation KPIs and SLAs; lead monthly and quarterly business reviews (QBRs) with 3PL and carrier partners to drive accountability and continuous improvement.

· Serve as the primary escalation point for transportation service failures; root-cause issues and implement corrective and preventive actions.

· Ensure transportation execution meets the requirements of key retail partners (e.g., compliance with retailer routing guides, delivery windows, and ASN/labeling standards).

Cost Review & Optimization

· Own the regional transportation budget and freight spend; forecast, monitor, and explain variances monthly, identifying trends and driving corrective action.

· Conduct regular cost-to-serve analysis across lanes, modes, and channels; identify and implement opportunities to reduce cost per unit without compromising service.

· Lead carrier rate negotiations, spot-market management, and freight procurement in coordination with the US Director of Transportation and procurement team.

· Evaluate mode and lane optimization, consolidation, and network design changes to deliver year-over-year cost savings.

3PL Capacity & Growth Strategy

· Develop and maintain a forward-looking transportation capacity strategy that aligns with e.l.f.'s aggressive international growth plans, modeling 1-, 3-, and 5-year volume scenarios against 3PL and carrier capability.

· Assess the scalability of existing 3PL partners — across warehousing throughput, outbound capacity, peak-season flex, and geographic coverage — and recommend capacity additions, alternate partners, or network changes ahead of need.

· Lead or support RFPs, partner selection, onboarding, and contract governance for new or expanded 3PL and carrier relationships across the UK and EU.

· Build peak-season and surge-readiness plans in partnership with 3PLs, ensuring capacity, labor, and equipment commitments are secured well in advance of demand spikes (e.g., holiday, promotional events, new-retailer launches).

· Identify and mitigate supply chain risks — carrier concentration, single-lane dependency, customs/border exposure — with documented contingency plans.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Compliance

· Partner with the US Associate Director of Transportation to ensure regional execution aligns with global transportation strategy, systems, and standards (e.g., TMS, visibility platforms, carrier scorecards).

· Collaborate with Supply Planning, Demand Planning and Commercial Operations to align transportation capacity with forecasted demand and product launch timelines.

· Ensure full compliance with UK and EU transportation, customs, and trade regulations, and partner with customs brokers to maintain efficient and compliant cross-border movement.

· Champion e.l.f.'s sustainability commitments in transportation decisions, including modal shift, emissions reduction, and carrier sustainability standards.

Requirements:

· Lead the transportation strategy working with the other operations team professionals, building capability and a culture of continuous improvement.

· Act as the regional transportation subject-matter expert and represent the function in cross-functional initiatives and leadership reviews.

· Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

· 5+ years of progressive experience in transportation, logistics, or 3PL management, with at least 3 years in a leadership role.

· Demonstrated experience managing 3PL relationships and carrier networks at scale, including SLA governance, QBRs, and performance management.

· Strong financial acumen — proven ownership of a transportation or freight budget, cost-to-serve analysis, and rate negotiation.

· Deep working knowledge of UK and EU transportation markets, carrier landscapes, customs/trade compliance, and retail routing-guide requirements.

· Experience planning capacity or network strategy to support significant volume growth.

Closing:

It also reflects the general details considered necessary to describe the principal functions of the job identified, and shall not be considered, as detailed description of all the work required inherent in the job. It is not an exhaustive list of responsibilities, and it is subject to changes and exceptions at the supervisors’ discretion.

The base salary range for this role is listed above. 
 
Total compensation includes base salary, annual company-based performance bonus, and equity. Under e.l.f.’s annual bonus program, employees are eligible to earn up to 200% of their target bonus when company performance exceeds defined goals. In addition, e.l.f. provides a variety of other benefits to employees, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a retirement savings plan, gender neutral parental leave, and unlimited paid time off. The amount of total compensation (including base salary) offered will be based on a wide range of factors, including geographic location, experience, specific skills, and qualifications.

raw.title: Product Marketing Lead
raw.description:
Product Marketing Lead

Reporting to: CMO

Location: London (hybrid, 4 days a week in the office)

Salary: £80,000-£100,000 + equity

About Electric Twin

Most organisations make their biggest decisions on a thin slice of evidence - a handful of customer calls, one survey, instinct when the data runs out. Electric Twin changes that. We build synthetic audiences: simulations of real groups of people, grounded in research data. Teams ask them questions, test ideas and explore how people might respond, and get answers in minutes that would otherwise take weeks.

The work is grounded, and the science is real. We've run over 40,000 evaluations across populations covering 155 countries. Independent academic research with Professor Michael Muthukrishna at the LSE found our outputs come back roughly 10,000x faster than traditional methods, at 95% accuracy. Customers including The Times, Sage, Virgin, Vodafone and Wingstop use Electric Twin to bring customer insight into decisions about campaigns, products, pricing and strategy.

Electric Twin was founded by Dr Ben Warner (former Chief Data Advisor to the UK Prime Minister) and our CEO, Alex Cooper (a former senior military commander and Director of Mass Covid Testing in the pandemic). We're backed by Atomico, LocalGlobe, Mercuri and angels including Marc Andreessen. We're a team of engineers, AI researchers, behavioural scientists and operators - careful with the science, careful with the responsibility.

The role

We're hiring a Product Marketing Lead to own product marketing at Electric Twin, from the strategy through to the sales deck.

Our ambition is to make understanding people a normal part of making decisions. Product marketing is central to that. It's how we decide who Electric Twin is for, what we compete against and why a buyer should choose us, and how that story reaches the market through our product, our website and our sales team.

Next year is a big one. We're launching in new markets, taking Electric Twin to more parts of a business, and bringing more products to market. We need someone who has operated at this level before, and who can join the dots between sales, marketing and product.

Product marketing here covers four areas: insights, storytelling, go-to-market and enablement. You'll own all four, and decide where to lean in as the company grows.

You'll work closely with our CMO, our VP Product and our sales team. Our Growth Lead runs the engine - the channels and programmes that reach and convert our audience. Product marketing and content provide the fuel. You'll own positioning and messaging. Our Content Lead will turn it into stories and get them out across every channel.

This is a hands-on role. You'll set the strategy, and you'll also write the launch plan, the value proposition brief and the sales deck yourself.

What’s exciting - you’re the founding PMM and get to build out and lead this function as we expand.

What you'll do

Insights

  • Be the expert on our customer. We have strong customer research, a map of what customers want to use the product for and a regular round-up of the questions they ask. Build on it, keep it current and make sure the rest of the business uses it.

  • Understand the buyers we're growing into. Our buyer today is the insights team. Marketing, product and commercial teams come next. Speak to them, define who they are and work out what they need to hear from us.

  • Know the market. This is a fast-moving category, with research incumbents launching their own products and a new batch of innovators arriving. Track it, and keep a clear, committed point of view on how Electric Twin is different.

  • Bring an opinion to product strategy. Work with our VP Product on the value proposition, and bring the customer and the market into decisions about what we build.

Storytelling

  • Own our positioning and messaging. Keep one consistent way of describing what Electric Twin is, who it is for and why a buyer should choose it, used by sales, product and marketing.

  • Own the trust story. Trust is central to how buyers choose us. Own how we prove it: the evidence, the customer stories and the guidance for prospects who want to evaluate us for themselves.

  • Turn the product into language a buyer would use. Take what we build and describe it in the customer's words, across the website, the product and our sales materials.

  • Shape the story for new markets and buyers. Build and adjust the narrative for our new market launches, and for the teams beyond insight and research that we want to reach.

Go-to-market

  • Set the product narrative. Agree a product narrative each quarter with our VP Product, so every launch adds up to a bigger story.

  • Run our launches. Build a tiered launch process so the effort matches the size of the release, and run it with product, sales and marketing.

  • Take Electric Twin to new buyers and markets. Plan how we go to market in the US, in new verticals and with new teams inside our customers.

  • Improve the buyer journey on our website. Work with growth, content and design so the site shows the product and has something for visitors who aren't yet ready to talk to sales.

Enablement

  • Equip our sales team. A sales deck built on our positioning, battlecards for the alternatives that come up most, ROI material for the economic buyer and a pack our champions can take to their senior stakeholders.

  • Build a working relationship with sales. Agree priorities together, with one route in for requests and a short brief for each.

  • Train sales and CX. Run onboarding and regular training on our positioning, product, use cases and objection handling, so both teams can explain our value and help customers get the most from Electric Twin.

  • Build feedback loops across teams. Create regular workflows that bring sales objections, win/loss insights and CX feedback into product priorities, positioning and enablement. Take updates back to those teams and check whether they solve the problems raised.

  • Be an advocate inside the business. Present to the company, and represent the customer and the product in the conversations that matter. You need to be the central point between Sales, Marketing and Product and drive the strategy proactively to each - ultimately for the benefit of the customer.

  • Build our product marketing operating system. Bring our research, positioning and messaging into one managed source of truth that feeds the tools used across product, sales, customer success and internal comms. Use AI to build repeatable workflows on top of it and keep it updated.

Your first six months

  • Take our positioning and messaging and get it into the website, sales enablement and our core external-facing materials.

  • Agree the first quarterly product narrative with our VP Product, and get a tiered launch process running.

  • Rebuild sales enablement, with battlecards, ROI material and a pack for champions.

  • Define the marketing buyer and build the narrative for our new market launches.

  • Get the product marketing operating system up and running.

What we're looking for

Experience

  • At least five years in product marketing alone. You've done this role before, ideally growing a product in a similar space or selling to an enterprise audience.

  • You've owned positioning and messaging, and taken it through to a website and sales materials that people used.

  • You've run product launches with a product team, and worked closely with a sales team on what they need to win deals.

  • You've partnered with senior product and commercial leaders, and you're as comfortable having an opinion on product strategy as on sales and commercial strategy.

  • You understand the tools and techniques of the trade, including Jobs-to-be-done and know how to define messaging and positioning.

Skills and approach

  • Autonomous. You can own the strategy and ship the copy without much steering. .

  • A good writer, and strong at the content specific to product marketing, such as sales decks and value proposition briefs.

  • A strong communicator. You can present internally and be an advocate for the customer and the product.

  • Curious and proactive. You know what you don't know, you read up or ask for help, and you act on problems once you've spotted them.

  • You've used AI to build repeatable workflows, and you can judge when the output is good enough and when it isn't.

  • You can operate in a fast-paced environment that has ambiguity.

  • You work with a sense of urgency, you raise issues as they arise and you anticipate problems

  • Careful with the details. You're comfortable getting to grips with AI, research and technical subjects, you ask good questions and you check claims carefully.

What we offer

  • £80,000-£100,000 base

  • Meaningful equity in a high-potential seed-stage company

  • Unlimited leave. Take the time you need

  • Generous matched pension contributions

  • Private healthcare

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Ownership of product marketing, with real influence over how the function is built

  • Direct access to and collaboration with world-class founders

  • Hybrid working from our London office (4 days in office a week)

  • Flexible working around life commitments. We value outcomes over presenteeism

When you apply, please share examples of your product marketing work, such as positioning, a launch or sales materials, explaining your contribution and what it achieved.

raw.title: Merchandise Planning & Analytics Analyst
raw.description:
Farfetch is a leading global marketplace for the luxury fashion industry, connecting customers in over 190 countries with items from more than 50 countries and over 1,400 of the world’s best brands and charming boutiques from around the world. Farfetch opens a world of luxury for endless expressions of style, delivering a truly unique shopping experience and access to the most extensive selection of luxury on a global marketplace. 

LONDON
Our London office is located in Old Street, London’s tech hub, and is home to a wide range of teams. Our open space is ideal for collaborative work and sharing ideas. We also have a large outdoor terrace, which is the perfect spot to have a team lunch or host events.

COMMERICAL
We're partnering with global brands and the most influential and renowned boutique curators to bring our customers an unrivalled range of fashion to empower their individuality. We’re relationship builders, we’re solution finders and we’re analysts. We work with all areas of the FARFETCH business to improve our social and environmental impact while delivering business success. We want to empower our consumers to buy better, improve our operational footprint, and explore new business models that improve our impact. 

THE ROLE
The Merchandise Planning & Analytics team supports the growth of key supply channels and brand partnerships on FARFETCH through commercial planning and data-driven insights.
As a Merchandise Planning & Analytics Analyst, you will support the team in analysing business performance, identifying opportunities to optimise supply and maximising sales. You will contribute to pre-season planning and in-season trading, while developing analytical tools and processes to support better commercial decision-making.
Working closely with colleagues across Brand Partnerships, Business Development, Online Merchandising, Marketing, Operations, Product and Business Insights, you will help translate data into actionable insights and recommendations.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Analytics

  • Analyse sales, stock and demand performance across brands, channels, regions, categories and products, identifying key trends and commercial opportunities.

  • Produce actionable insights and recommendations to optimise supply, improve product availability and maximise sales.

  • Develop and maintain dashboards, reports and analytical tools, working with BI and other technical teams to improve business visibility.

  • Support analysis of key commercial initiatives, including markdown optimisation, next-day delivery and exclusive products.

  • Present findings through regular trade meetings, business reviews and project updates.

  • Support with ad-hoc analysis and requests from senior management and business development

    • Planning

  • Support Merchandise Planning & Analytics managers in pre-season planning for key brand partners, using historical performance and demand trends to inform supply and assortment recommendations.

  • Refresh and maintain sales forecasting and planning models, supporting target setting and scenario analysis.

  • Monitor sales and stock performance against targets and forecasts, identifying risks and opportunities.

  • Identify supply opportunities and recommend actions to improve product availability and maximise sales.

  • Support ongoing forecasting and planning updates, contributing to the development of more effective planning models and processes


    • WHO YOU ARE

  • Collaborative, flexible and approachable, with pride in the quality of your work and an understanding that how you work is just as important as what you deliver.

  • Previous experience in Merchandise Planning, Buying, Demand or Supply Planning, Analytics or Consulting, ideally within the fashion or luxury industry.

  • An understanding of the fashion and luxury industry and its commercial drivers.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience in data analysis using large data sets .

  • Excellent planning and organisational skills, with strong attention to detail.

  • Commercially minded, with the ability to translate data into actionable insights.

  • Proactive and curious, with the ability to identify opportunities and challenge existing ways of working.

  • Comfortable managing competing priorities and working to deadlines in a fast-paced environment, ability to escalate challenges to management

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the understanding of how  present findings clearly to different audiences.

  • Technical skills for processing and analysing large amounts of data:

  • Excel (mid level) and SQL (preferred, basic level) .

  • Looker or equivalent BI tools (desirable).


    • REWARDS & BENEFITS
  • Employee Pension Scheme
  • Flexible Benefits Program
  • Health Insurance & Critical Illness cover
  • Flexible work environment (3 days a week in office, 2 days WFH)

raw.description:
About Freetrade

Freetrade’s mission is to become the default place to invest. Investing has been too complicated and expensive for too long, keeping millions from making the most of their savings.

We’re changing that.

We’re building our team and looking for people who are excited to reshape how our customers invest and grow their wealth. If you’re driven by solving complex problems and building innovative products, you’ll fit right in.

2026 is a big year for us. Last year, we announced a game changing deal to become part of the IG Group. We’ll continue to operate as an independent business while gaining access to the resources and support of an established leader in the space.

This year, we’re accelerating our roadmap and taking our products to the next level. We’re building new features like mutual funds, bonds, and family investment tools. We’re also exploring how we can leverage AI to deliver an even better experience for our customers.

Why join the Commercial Finance team at Freetrade?

You will be joining a small Commercial Finance team on a 6-month Fixed Term Contract (FTC) as Freetrade enters the ‘scale-up’ phase of its business. Our team is evolving from an FP&A reporting team to a commercial-oriented business partnering team. You will be providing commercial insight through impactful and insightful analysis to influence executive-level decision-making. You will report to the Head of Commercial Finance.

You will:

  • Partner with our marketing leadership team, along with additional central departments

  • Proactively highlight opportunities for efficiency, evaluating value for money, reviewing paybacks, CACs and ROIs

  • Provide commercial challenge and recommendations, from both data analysis and competitor scanning

  • Seek continuous improvement in reporting, finding areas for automation and opportunities to create self-serve dashboards

  • Own the annual budget for your area along with monthly reporting against budget

  • Forecast headcount spend in partnership with department heads in order to drive hiring decisions

  • Forecast vendor-level spend, track renewal dates and run supplier negotiations

  • Prepare models for business cases, projecting costs and impact for new products, new suppliers and new operations

Experience:

  • Recognised accounting qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent) with 5+ years of relevant experience, including 3+ years as a Finance Business Partner.

  • Experience working in financial services/fintech or similar industries

  • Experience of business partnering with a marketing function

  • Experience in building financial models and conducting scenario analysis

About you:

  • A proactive, self-motivated problem solver

  • An effective communicator with the ability to build strong relationships across all levels of the company

  • An interest in the investments industry

  • Highly numerate

Benefits & Logistics

Freetrade is the place to accelerate your career. Our benefits package and ways of working are designed to attract and retain the most talented people who are dedicated to making an impact at Freetrade.

Here’s what’s on offer in 2026:

Hybrid working culture


We’re operating in a hybrid model: 3-days in-office / 2-days from home. We believe great collaboration happens in person and our beautiful offices in central London and Budapest are designed to bring people together.


🏢 Office days: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday
🏡 Work from home days: Wednesday, Friday

This setup helps us stay connected, collaborate more effectively, and keep building a culture where we all do our best work together, including dedicated days for focus work.

Flexibility for those who need it:

We have a hybrid working model, but life happens. If you need flexibility let's talk about it, whether you're a parent or have other care responsibilities.

Values - at Freetrade we live and breathe our values: Honesty, Focus and Grit. Expect to be asked about these in your interview!

Benefits In London:

  • Competitive salary – carefully benchmarked.

  • Holidays – 25 days plus UK public holidays. Your birthday off, plus one extra day for every year at Freetrade.

  • Enhanced pension – We’ll match your contributions up to 7%.

  • Group Life Insurance – Protect your loved ones with coverage at 5x your salary, ensuring financial security in any circumstance.

  • Private Health Insurance - Which includes access to high quality medical care, mental health support, dental and vision plans, Wellness programs and preventative care initiatives are also provided to ensure the wellbeing of your entire family.

  • Bonus Scheme - join us and share in our growth. Bonuses are linked to both company success and your individual impact.

  • Income Protection Cover – Safeguard your income with comprehensive coverage, ensuring financial stability in the event of illness or injury.

  • Enhanced parental leave – Time off when it matters most. ** Eligibility is subject to length of service and statutory requirements.

  • Flexibility for those who need it – We’re office-first, but life happens. Whether you’re a parent or have care responsibilities, we focus on output and trust you to manage your time.

  • Learning & Development – We fund industry qualifications so you can grow as a financial services professional.

  • Cycle to Work scheme – Get a high quality bike and gear through our salary sacrifice scheme, spreading the cost with tax free monthly installments.

  • Paid Sick Leave – Receive 10 days of fully paid sick leave each calendar year.

Interview Process
We keep things simple and transparent. Our process typically includes:

  1. Initial interview – A chat with one of our Talent Partners.

  2. Hiring Manager interview – A deep dive into your skills and experience.

  3. Values interview – A conversation with our stakeholders, where we also assess cultural fit.

We are an Equal Opportunity employer committed to a diverse and representative team. Whatever your race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability - we want to hear from you.

raw.title: Application Security Engineer
raw.description:
Location: Oxford or London (Hybrid)

The Mission: Why We Exist

Genomics is a science-led transatlantic TechBio combining large-scale genetic and health data with proprietary analytics to accelerate drug discovery and advance predictive, preventative healthcare. We are united by a single vision to help people live longer, healthier lives, using the power of genomics.

Genomics aims to help people live longer, healthier lives in two ways: super-charging drug discovery and development for novel treatments with our AI-enabled advanced genetic analytics platform, and by helping people understand their personal risk of common chronic diseases through polygenic risk scores - giving doctors and health systems the chance to get the right people into the right prevention, screening and treatment programmes at the right time.

Role Purpose

Genomic data is some of the most sensitive data there is, and our customers trust us with it. As Senior Application Security Engineer on Mystra, you'll own application security end-to-end across multi-tenant, trillion-row-scale, AI-enabled data platforms.

You'll lead threat modelling and design review with product teams, build the tooling and patterns that make secure codet, and find and fix the vulnerabilities that slip through. You'll do it with security-focused AI tooling, steered by your own expert judgement and intuition, to keep Genomics secure against state-of-the-art threats.

A Day in the Life

  • Leading threat modelling and design reviews for new products and infrastructure, and defining the security invariants every team builds against: tenant isolation, authentication and authorisation, secrets, least privilege, and trust boundaries

  • Building the libraries, patterns, and CI/CD guardrails that make the secure way the easy way, and deciding what is enforced versus advised

  • Building and tuning AI tooling for code analysis, triage, and remediation, and deciding where its output can be trusted and where it must be verified

  • Hunting for vulnerabilities through code review, testing, and proof-of-concept exploits, then running the disclosure programme and driving every finding through to a verified fix

  • Securing our agentic and AI surfaces, from prompt injection and tool boundaries to delegated credentials and tenant-scoped access, and proving the controls hold under adversarial testing

  • Working as an embedded, trusted partner to product teams, SRE, detection and response, the data platform team, and the MystraAI / ML team, unblocking rather than gating

Who You Are

  • Experience within application security in production. You've found and fixed exploitable bugs in software you were responsible for, through threat modelling, secure design, code review, and proof-of-concept exploitation across web services, APIs, and data-serving interfaces. Triaging scanner output doesn't count

  • Production-quality software engineering in at least one mainstream language (such as Python, Go, or TypeScript), and you can read several. You've built and operated security or developer tooling in CI/CD pipelines, such as static and dependency analysis, secrets detection, or policy-as-code, and engineers actually adopted it

  • Hands-on depth securing multi-tenant systems on a major cloud. We run on AWS (RDS, EC2, S3, EKS, Batch), and comparable GCP or Azure depth transfers. You know tenant isolation, IAM and least privilege, secrets management, Kubernetes and container security, and the trust boundaries between services

  • Daily use of frontier AI models for code analysis, vulnerability triage, remediation drafting, and research, with sharp judgement about where they're reliable and where they mislead. You've built or tuned LLM-driven tooling rather than only used a chat interface, and you understand the attack surface it introduces

  • Experience running, or being core to, a vulnerability disclosure or bug bounty programme and the remediation lifecycle behind it, covering severity, prioritisation, SLAs, root cause, and systemic fixes. You've also worked application-layer incidents alongside detection and response, using security telemetry and SIEM data as evidence

  • Risk-led judgement. You know which designs need deep review, which findings matter and which are noise, and you make accepted risk explicit so leadership can decide with open eyes

  • Clear communication. You explain risk and trade-offs precisely to engineers, product, and leadership, write guidance people actually use, and mentor others to grow security capability across teams

Your Package

We are committed to providing a transparent, supportive, and rewarding work environment.

Compensation & Growth

  • Competitive Reward: Salaries are externally benchmarked annually to ensure market-aligned compensation.

  • Clear Career Path: A straightforward, open progression framework means you'll always know the path to promotion and how to achieve your next career goal.

  • Continuous Learning: Including external courses and a wide library of L&D materials, because your growth is our success.

Wellbeing & Time Off

  • Holiday: 25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays, plus an extra 3-day company-wide shutdown at year-end.

  • Financial & Health Security: Robust benefits including a market-leading pension scheme, comprehensive private health insurance for you and your family with NO excess, critical illness, and life assurance.

  • Enhanced Leave: Enhanced paid family leave to support all new parents.

Work Environment & Culture

  • Hybrid Working

  • Truly Inclusive Time Off: Our 'Bank Your Bank Holiday' program allows you to exchange public holidays for dates that hold personal or cultural significance to you.

  • Vibrant Social Culture: From regular Town Halls and team picnics to organised sports events, our social committee ensures frequent opportunities to connect and celebrate.

  • Green Commute: Cycle-to-Work scheme and convenient office locations near major transport hubs.

Ready to Build the Future?

If this opportunity excites you, apply now!

We are dedicated to creating a diverse environment and are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

Genomics politely requests no contact from recruitment agencies. We do not accept speculative CVs from recruitment agencies nor accept the fees associated with them.

raw.description:
At Hive, we're building the defining physical AI platform of the next decade.

Industrial labor is one of the most acute bottlenecks in the global economy. Operators are expensive, hard to retain, and working in environments that are increasingly unsafe. The shortage is structural. The window to solve it is now.

Our answer is a machine-agnostic intelligence platform that lets any machine, on any site, perceive, decide, and act autonomously. One platform. Any machine. No fleet replacement.

Already live across multiple sites and customers in Europe - spanning logistics and warehousing, industrial manufacturing, and large-scale chemical production - with a US expansion underway.

The vision: one operator managing hundreds of machines simultaneously. Productive machine-hour cost dropping by 80x, and unlocks the next productivity revolution in physical work.

The mission is to make productivity limitless. Come and help us build it.

 

The role

We are looking for a pragmatic, field-oriented Operational Safety Advisor whose mission is to enable safe, efficient and repeatable deployments of autonomous industrial machines. Working within the Deployment team, you will help customers and Deployment Managers identify operational risks early, agree practical mitigations and remove blockers. Your role is to simplify how safety is addressed, not add bureaucracy, complexity or new approval gates.


Key responsibilities

Site visits and operational assessments

  • Visit customer sites to understand working practices, machine movements, pedestrian interfaces, traffic management, visibility and exclusion zones.

  • Identify operational risks early and work with customers and Deployment Managers to propose proportionate, practical actions that keep deployments moving safely.

The Ledger Platform team is rebuilding all of iwoca’s ledgers as one platform, starting with the ledger for the business credit card. Every card payment, loan repayment, and payout will end up there. Finance, Accounting, and Capital Markets rely on that record, so it has to be right every time.

The team is small – a principal engineer who leads it, another staff engineer, another engineer, and you. It works closely with the product teams that build on its ledgers, and with Finance.

The role

You'll lead projects from design to production, and decide with product what the team builds and how. With the principal engineer, you’ll set the platform’s technical direction, from service boundaries to the APIs and event streams other teams build on. Most of the platform is still to be built, and you’ll own part of it yourself. It’s a hands-on individual contributor role with high ownership and no line management.

Every payment a small business makes with iwoca crosses several services and network hops before it reaches the ledger, and any of them can fail. You'll build services that record each one exactly once, with no single point of failure, safe timeouts and retries, and graceful degradation when a dependency is down. When something breaks in production, you'll fix it so it doesn't break again.

You’ll learn iwoca’s financial products in depth, so you can challenge requirements and explain technical trade-offs to Finance. When the answer isn’t obvious, you’ll scope and prototype, and use domain modelling to find the simple design behind a complicated problem. You’ll influence which parts of a problem need solving now, which can wait, and which aren’t worth solving at all.

Live project examples:

  • New ledgers. Building the ledgers for Flexi-Loan and iwocaPay.

  • Account migration. Moving existing loan accounts onto the new ledgers with zero downtime and no data lost.

  • Credit card ledger. Building new features for the credit card ledger, from real-time card holds to daily interest and monthly statements.

  • Reconciliation and journals. Reconciling the ledger with banks, payment providers, and the card scheme, and producing the accounting journals Finance relies on.

  • Funding facilities. Recording how loans move between iwoca’s funding facilities.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Distributed systems. You’ve built and run fault-tolerant services in production, and handled the hard parts: durable communication between services, idempotency, transactional correctness, and partial failure.

  • Backend engineering. You have deep expertise in at least one object-oriented language. You’ve written and run backend services in it.

  • Databases. You’ve worked in depth with relational databases, ideally PostgreSQL, and solved data integrity, concurrency, and performance problems in them.

  • Ownership. You’ve led large projects across several engineers or teams, end to end, and helped other engineers grow through design and code reviews.

  • Testing. You’ve tested for edge cases and failures as carefully as you designed for them.

  • AI leverage. You’ve built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone, at work or in your own projects. You judge when to use it and when not to, and you check its output before it reaches production.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

  • Financial systems. You’ve built ledgers, billing, or payment systems, including the audit trails and reconciliation that prove they’re correct.

  • High volume. You’ve worked at a company where the volume of data or transactions shaped how you designed systems.

  • Migrations. You’ve moved live systems and data onto a new platform with zero downtime.

  • Python. You’ve used Python in production, with a web framework such as Django, FastAPI, or Flask. It’s the language the team works in.

  • Data tooling. You’ve built pipelines with Snowflake and dbt, or similar, that turn ledger data into reports for Finance.

  • Messaging. You’ve built asynchronous messaging with queues or topics, such as Kafka.

The salary

We expect to pay from £110,000 to £140,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

  • Interview welcome pack (TAP)

About Juicebox

Juicebox is on a mission to help teams win the talent war.

In the age of AI, human ingenuity is the ultimate scarce resource. Recruiting is a zero-sum game where you either compete or lose.

Teams at Ramp, Notion, and leading AI labs use Juicebox to power their hiring, alongside 5,000+ customers from early-stage startups to Fortune 500 companies.

We are on the path to $100M in ARR with 20%+ monthly growth, powering thousands of searches every day and making Juicebox one of the fastest-growing AI SaaS companies in the world.

Juicebox has raised over $116M in funding from lead investors including Sequoia Capital, DST Global, and NFDG. Read more about our $80M Series B here. Additional investors in Juicebox include Y Combinator, Coatue, Bond, Lux, Verified Capital, and Committed Capital.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Go-To-Market Recruiter to help build out our GTM teams. This isn’t a traditional recruiting role. Juicebox is an AI sourcing platform used by thousands of recruiters, founders, and talent leaders, you’ll become a visible leader in the recruiting community, working at the center of where modern sourcing and AI intersect.

You’ll help shape how we show up externally, through content, community, and candidate experience, to make Juicebox the top destination for top-tier talent in AI.

 

You’re a Fit If You…

  • Have 4+ years of experience recruiting (either in-house or agency)

  • Have a strong personal brand in the recruiting community (e.g., active LinkedIn presence, trusted network, respected by peers)

  • Have excellent written and verbal communication - you can make a candidate feel seen and understood

  • Thrive in fast-paced, zero-to-one environments

  • Care deeply about quality and candidate experience

  • Are excited to work in-office 5 days a week with the team in London

 

Bonus Points If You…

  • Have worked with early-stage startups (Seed - Series B) or in-house at high-growth companies

  • Familiar with AI, SaaS, or B2B talent markets

  • Enjoy writing or speaking about hiring, talent, or the future of work

Perks & Benefits for all Full Time Employees

  • Top-of-market compensation with meaningful equity, because everyone should share in our success.

  • Daily meals provided: breakfast catering, lunch order via DoorDash corporate, and for those who like to work late, dinner if staying after 7pm

For US Employees:

  • Comprehensive healthcare with 100% employer-paid medical coverage for employees (PPO Platinum plan with $0 deductible). 90% employer contribution for dependents. Dental & Vision: 90% employer covered; 85% for dependents.

  • $2,000 annual wellness stipend to support your physical, mental, and financial well-being.

  • $300/month commuting stipend to help cover the cost of getting to and from the office.

For UK Employees:

  • Comprehensive private medical insurance with £0 excess, full outpatient cover, comprehensive cancer care, mental health treatment, and 24/7 GP access.

  • £1,500 annual wellness stipend to support your physical, mental, and financial well-being

  • £3,500/year commuting stipend to help cover the cost of getting to and from the office.

raw.title: People Coordinator
raw.description:
Location: London, UK (hybrid, three days a week in the office)

Level: C2

Team: People

Salary: £40,000 - £44,000 + discretionary bonus

Contract: Permanent

Reporting To: People Experience Manager

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.


About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

 

What you’ll do

  • Own the People service desk queue day-to-day: triaging, responding to, and resolving employee queries, and keeping response times and queue health on track.

  • Continuously improve our Jira Service Desk itself - refining triage, workflows, and automations - and feed recurring ticket themes back into our People Bot's knowledge base, so the answers people get before they ever need a human just keep getting better.

  • Be the main point of contact for new joiners between offer and day one, partnering with Talent Acquisition to make pre-boarding seamless and ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.

  • Own and continuously improve the onboarding experience end-to-end - from offer acceptance to day one and beyond - so every new hire feels genuinely welcomed and set up for success.

  • Support payroll inputs, benefits administration, and compliance activities, making sure our processes hold up against internal policy and employment law requirements.

  • Help audit and redesign People processes, spotting where automation, AI, or self-service can reduce manual effort and put information directly in employees' hands.

  • Partner with the wider People team on cross-functional projects, from Reward cycles to hiring initiatives and employee experience improvements, bringing structure and good coordination to keep things moving.


What you’ll bring

Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Proven experience in a People Operations or HR administrative role, with a genuine interest in how operational rigour underpins the employee lifecycle.

  • Hands-on experience with a HRIS, ideally Workday - confident keeping records accurate and up to date across onboarding and lifecycle changes.

  • A curious, detail-oriented approach to data - you notice when something looks off, dig into why, and flag it.

  • Experience with payroll input processes, and the attention to detail that accurate processing demands.

  • Experience administering employee benefits (enrolment, changes, queries), and a go-to point of contact when something needs sorting.

  • A track record of spotting clunky processes and making them better - you ask why things work the way they do, and you suggest or build improvements.

  • Experience running a queue in a service desk tool (Jira or similar), with good instincts for prioritising, keeping things moving and knowing what to escalate.

  • Working knowledge of UK employment law and compliance, and the judgment to know when to act and when to flag.

  • Clear, warm communication - equally comfortable writing to a nervous new joiner as flagging something to a manager.


What will set you apart:

  • You're curious about what AI and automation can do for People Operations. You're already trying out tools, forming opinions, and bringing ideas back to the team rather than waiting to be asked.

  • You hold yourself to a high bar, and when you see something that could be better, you say so and take the lead on fixing it.

  • You share what you know and keep people in the loop, so a new joiner never feels like they're chasing you for answers.


Tech stack: Workday, Jira


Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

 

Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.
