The Role

We're looking for a dedicated Account Manager to own and accelerate expansion across our existing customer base. This is a high-impact, commercial role for someone who thrives on closing six- to seven-figure deals with enterprise teams.


We've grown fast without dedicated expansion resources, but the opportunity is massive. Our team has identified millions of dollars in qualified pipeline, and we need a closer who can convert it.

You'll own a book of business worth $2M+ ARR across high-growth mid-market and enterprise companies (~400-8,000 employees), managing complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles from discovery through close. You'll be measured on Net Revenue Retention and your ability to execute consultative, value-based selling at scale.

Important to know:

  • Hours: This is an exciting but intense job. Kernel is growing extremely fast and hours can often be long. Many of our customers are on the West Coast, and meetings can be held late in the evening.

  • Working location: Minimum 4 days a week in the London office (Borough). Most people do 5.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Own and execute complex expansion and renewal cycles across a $2M+ book of mid-market and enterprise accounts, managing deals from six- to seven figures with technical, multi-stakeholder buying groups.

  • Drive Net Revenue Retention by proactively identifying expansion opportunities, negotiating renewals, and preventing churn across your portfolio. You'll be commercially accountable for growing the revenue in your book.

  • Execute consultative, value-based selling by deeply understanding each customer's RevOps challenges, articulating clear ROI, and positioning Kernel as mission-critical infrastructure for their CRM data strategy.

  • Own the full customer relationship alongside Implementation/Solutions Engineers, proactively sourcing expansion opportunities through account mapping, strategic outreach, and deep engagement with your accounts to identify growth potential.

  • Build and refine our Account Management playbook as a key member of our growing Account Management team, helping establish repeatable processes for expansion motions, renewal cadences, and cross-functional collaboration that will scale with the team as we grow

  • Partner cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, and GTM leadership to shape our expansion strategy, feed critical customer insights into the product roadmap, and help define our enterprise selling motion.

  • Navigate complex contracts, security reviews, and legal discussions independently, moving deals forward without constant support from leadership or legal.

More specifically, you will be:

  • Speaking the language of RevOps professionals, discussing CRM hierarchies, data hygiene, territory planning, and the technical challenges of managing company data at scale.

  • Becoming the best person in the company at explaining and pitching the product, translating technical capabilities into clear business value for VP-level stakeholders.

  • Running data-driven account reviews and strategic planning sessions to prioritize where to invest your time for maximum revenue impact.

What You Bring

  • Proven track record of expansion and renewal excellence: 4-7 years of B2B SaaS sales or account management experience, with at least 2 years consistently closing $100k+ deals per year and managing a book of business worth $2M+ ARR.

  • Demonstrable commercial performance: You have a track record of consistently overachieving on Net Revenue Retention or expansion targets (130%+ NRR is the bar), with specific examples of closing significant expansions from existing customers. You're commercially driven and performance-oriented, motivated by hitting and exceeding revenue targets, and you understand the levers that drive expansion and renewal.

  • Enterprise sales expertise: Experience navigating complex, multi-stakeholder sales processes with technical buyers. You know how to manage 6-12 month sales cycles, build consensus across buying committees, and close six-figure deals.

  • Consultative selling and communication skills: You can execute value-based, solutions-oriented selling, asking great questions to uncover true business pain and positioning product capabilities as strategic solutions rather than features. You have excellent verbal and written communication skills - you articulate complex ideas crisply, write compelling proposals and business cases, and present confidently to senior stakeholders.

  • Technical fluency: Comfortable discussing technical concepts with RevOps and data teams. You can translate complex requirements into product demonstrations and articulate technical value to non-technical executives.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset: You thrive in ambiguity and are energized by building processes from scratch. You're a generalist who can wear multiple hats, take ownership beyond your job description, and move fast without perfect clarity.

  • Operational independence: You can navigate contracts, negotiate terms, handle security questionnaires, and move deals through legal and procurement without needing constant support from leadership.

It is a plus if you also have:

  • Background in data infrastructure, CRM platforms, or API-first products.

  • Startup or scale-up experience (Series A-C), where you've seen a commercial function built from the ground up.

  • Familiarity with Salesforce.

⚠️ This role may not be for you if you:

  • Struggle with technical stakeholders: Our customers are RevOps professionals who speak CRM, data models, and API integrations. If you're not comfortable learning and discussing technical concepts, you won't be able to build credibility.

  • Expect consistent 9-5 hours: With West Coast customers and the intensity of a fast-growing startup, this role requires flexibility and often long hours. If work-life balance is your top priority, this isn't the right fit.

❌ This role is definitely not for you if you:

  • Haven't consistently hit commercial targets: If you don't have a track record of meeting or exceeding expansion and renewal quotas, or if you've never managed a significant book of business, you'll struggle with the commercial accountability this role requires.

  • Prefer individual contributor work without cross-functional collaboration: This role requires constant coordination with Customer Success, Product, and Engineering. If you prefer to work in isolation, this won't be a good fit.

What We Offer

We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.

  • 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays

  • 🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace

Head of Sales, Dave Bentham

Account Manager, Lewis Goode

raw.title: Account Manager – Maritime Data & Technology Providers – Europe
raw.description:
At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors.
 
Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 850 experts from 69 countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success.
 

Join a team that turns the complexity of global trade into something anyone can build on. You’ll work with data providers, software and technology companies, consultancies, and education and research organisations across Europe. These are clients who embed or build on Kpler’s maritime intelligence in their own products, platforms and services, rather than using it only internally.




Key Responsibilities

  • Drive revenue growth across your European portfolio of non-end-user accounts, meeting or exceeding annual targets.

  • Understand how each client plans to use the data: embedded in a product, redistributed, displayed, or used in research and consulting work. Shape the right licensing and product fit around that use.

  • Work with the Partnership team and Legal on non-end-user approvals and contract terms. Spot non-end-user situations early and follow internal processes.

  • Identify and close upsell and cross-sell opportunities as clients’ products and data needs evolve.

  • Act as a commercial business partner on planning, forecasting and key metrics, and keep Salesforce accurate to support reliable forecasting.

  • Maintain a clear, consistent pipeline every quarter to ensure transparency and achieve quota.

  • Discuss APIs, data feeds and integrations with clients’ product and engineering teams, working with Kpler’s technical teams where needed.

  • Gather market, product and competitor intelligence from clients to inform Kpler’s product and commercial strategy.

  • Negotiate contracts and commercial terms in line with company policy.

  • Collaborate with Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Sales Operations, Business Units and Business Development, and represent Kpler externally with credibility.


    • Experience & Background

    What you'll need (Must-haves):

  • 2+ years of B2B sales or account management experience, ideally selling data, APIs, SaaS or other technology products.

  • Comfort working with clients who are themselves data, software, consulting or research organisations, and who build on or resell what they buy.

  • Experience managing and growing a portfolio of accounts, with a track record of retaining and expanding relationships.

  • Comfort discussing technical topics (APIs, data feeds, integrations) with product and engineering stakeholders, and a willingness to learn quickly.

  • Strong communication, consultative and negotiation skills, with full professional fluency in English.

  • Self-motivation, resilience and adaptability in a fast-paced environment.

    • Nice-to-haves:

  • Knowledge of maritime shipping, global trade or commodities markets.

  • Experience with complex or non-standard licensing, partnerships or reseller models.

  • Proficiency with Salesforce and modern sales tools (e.g. LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Outreach, ZoomInfo).

  • Working proficiency in French, German or other European languages.

  • Willingness to travel for key client meetings and industry events.

    • We are a dynamic company dedicated to nurturing connections and innovating solutions to tackle market challenges head-on. If you thrive on customer satisfaction and turning ideas into reality, then you’ve found your ideal destination. Are you ready to embark on this exciting journey with us?
     
    We make things happen
    We act decisively and with purpose, going the extra mile.
     
    We build together
    We foster relationships and develop creative solutions to address market challenges.
     
    We are here to help
    We are accessible and supportive to colleagues and clients with a friendly approach.
     
     
    Our People Pledge
     
    Don’t meet every single requirement? Research shows that women and people of color are less likely than others to apply if they feel like they don’t match 100% of the job requirements. Don’t let the confidence gap stand in your way, we’d love to hear from you! We understand that experience comes in many different forms and are dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team.
     
    Kpler is committed to providing a fair, inclusive and diverse work-environment. We believe that different perspectives lead to better ideas, and better ideas allow us to better understand the needs and interests of our diverse, global community. We welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives and are an equal opportunity employer.
     
     
     
    By applying, I confirm that I have read and accept the Staff Privacy Notice

raw.title: Chief of Staff
raw.description:
Reports directly to the Founder & CEO · Letly & Aravis

We are building a vertically integrated AI-native property operations and financial services business serving landlords and tenants. We’re hiring a Chief of Staff to own Finance, Risk and Strategy & Operations across both businesses.

Working directly with the CEO, you’ll help decide where we invest, manage the risks we take and turn ambitious plans into results. You’ll have substantial responsibility and accountability from the outset.

You will own:

  • Finance: Lead budgeting, forecasting, cash management, financial reporting and unit economics. Oversee accounting and financial controls, manage external advisers, and lead the financial preparation for fundraising and board reporting.

  • Risk: Build and maintain risk policies, limits and reporting. Own the commercial framework for Secured underwriting and pricing, monitor portfolio performance and exposure, and drive corrective action. Work with compliance and other specialists on risk across Aravis.

  • StratOps: Translate company strategy into priorities, targets and accountable owners. Evaluate new opportunities, pricing and investment decisions. Lead critical initiatives across teams, resolve obstacles and track results.

  • Systems: Build reliable processes using data, automation and AI, keeping these functions effective as the business scales.

You’ll bring:

  • Strong financial skills: you can build models, interrogate accounts and understand cash flow and unit economics in detail.

  • The ability to solve problems rigorously from first principles, challenge assumptions and test conclusions against evidence.

  • A record of taking complex initiatives from analysis through to measurable results.

  • Commercial judgement: you can assess upside, quantify downside and make decisions with incomplete information.

  • Clear communication and the ability to hold people accountable across teams.

  • High agency, attention to detail and the intensity to deliver against demanding goals.

A STEM degree is desirable. Experience in fintech, financial services, underwriting or another business with material financial risk would be a strong advantage.

Success means reliable numbers, disciplined risk-taking and faster execution on the company’s most important priorities.

raw.title: Biosensor Research Scientist (Electrochemical sensors)
raw.description:
About Level Zero
 
Level Zero is pioneering next-generation biosensor technology for precise, real-time monitoring of critical endocrine biomarkers. Recognised as one of the top 20 startups across all categories worldwide at TechCrunch Disrupt 2024—and backed by top-tier organisations like SOSV and Entrepreneur First—we’re pushing the boundaries of biochemistry and nanotechnology to revolutionize personalised health.
 
Founded by two seasoned engineers, we bring extensive experience in R&D, technical innovation, and commercial strategy to transform the way people monitor their health. Our mission is bold: to revolutionise health management by delivering clinical-grade data directly to individuals, wherever they are.
 
We’re seeking driven innovators to join us in pushing the boundaries of biosensing and health tech, making personalised health monitoring a reality for everyone. To achieve this ambitious vision, we’re assembling the best team in the world—dedicated to turning cutting-edge science into life-changing, real-world solutions.
 
 
About the Role
 
We are excited to welcome a biosensor scientist with a strong background in electrochemical biosensor R&D and experience in working with aptamers to join our rapidly growing start-up. The ideal candidate is expected to be proficient in bench and wet chemistry techniques. Moreover, they should have sound knowledge and experience in assay development, small molecule detection, and electrode surface modifications. It is essential for the candidate to have extensive experience in aptamer-based electrochemical biosensor R&D, including the designs, operation principles, troubleshooting, and analysis.
 
This is a full-time, in-person role primarily based in London.
 
Some examples of what you might do:
 
- Design, prototype, and optimize electrochemical biosensor systems, focusing on small molecule analytes and aptamer-based recognition.
- Apply surface chemistry and electrode modification strategies to improve sensitivity, selectivity, stability, and biosensor performance in complex biological samples.
- Translate bio-element–target interactions into measurable and reproducible sensor outputs through novel assay design.
- Apply a range of electrochemical methods (voltammetry, impedimetry, chronoamperometry, etc.) to characterize and evaluate biosensor function.
- Apply data-driven approaches including Python-based analysis and Design of Experiments (DoE) to streamline workflows.
- Troubleshoot technical and conceptual challenges systematically and propose innovative solutions to improve performance.
- Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and ensure experimental reproducibility and compliance with quality standards.
- Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams (chemists, biologists, engineers, and data scientists) to advance biosensor prototypes from concept to application.
- Present results clearly through written reports, oral presentations, and scientific publications.
- Attend R&D-related trainings and seminars for continuous updates on the latest trend in hormone sensing technologies.
 

What You Bring
  • A Ph. D. degree in Electrochemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical/Materials Engineering or related discipline, with a focus in aptamer biosensors. Post doctoral experience will be a plus for this role.
    •  
    The ideal candidate will possess expertise in the following areas:
     
  • Proven hands-on experience in biosensor design, electrochemical techniques, and surface chemistry optimisation.
  • Proficiency in operating electrochemical instrumentation and analyzing experimental data.
  • Demonstrated expertise with biorecognition elements, particularly aptamers, for biosensor applications.
  • Strong knowledge of small molecule detection in biological and/or environmental samples.
  • Practical experience in handling and analyzing biofluids.
  • Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
  • Creative and open mindset with the ability to explore and implement novel approaches.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with experience working in multidisciplinary teams.
    •  
    Nice to have:
     
  • Experience with Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR), molecular docking, or structural modeling.
  • Familiarity with automation, Python scripting, and statistical design approaches (DoE).
  • Track record of peer-reviewed publications, patents, or industry-led biosensor projects.

    • Who You Are
  • We value culture as much as we value technical expertise, creating an environment that’s equal parts collaboration, curiosity, and fun.
    • We’re a fast-paced, mission-driven young team on a quest to make a lasting impact, fueled by uncompromising integrity, unwavering support for one another, and the thrill of exploring uncharted territories. Our passion for excellence drives everything we do, and we welcome individuals who share our commitment to shaping the future.
     
    If our vision excites you, here are the qualities we look for:
  • You live and breathe integrity, tackling challenges with honesty and transparency.
  • You’re a self-starter who loves diving into the unknown, collaborating on complex problems, and taking full ownership of results.
  • You excel at open, clear communication and see every piece of feedback as a springboard for growth—especially in a science and data-focused environment.
  • You’re motivated by creating real impact, particularly when it comes to advancing human health.
  • You strike a balance between independence and collaboration, knowing when to seek support or invite others to join in.
  • You’re confident in defending your ideas, while also valuing respectful, constructive debate as a path to better solutions.
  • You thrive in the dynamic atmosphere of a startup, constantly evolving your skill set and fearlessly applying what you learn.

    • What We Offer
  • A full-time role with a competitive salary and equity options, reflecting our value in your expertise and potential.
  • An environment where you’ll collaborate directly with the founding team at a leading biosensor startup, gaining access to industry experts and thought leaders.
  • The chance to grow with us, including ample opportunities for leadership, career advancement, and exploration.
  • Travel to New York and other potential sites for R&D purposes.
  • The excitement of working on cutting-edge technology, shaping strategic decisions, and driving innovation at an early-stage venture alongside a superstar team.
    • Be Part of Our Journey
     
    If you're ready to be at the forefront of biosensing innovation and thrive in fast-paced, learning-rich environments, we'd love to hear from you.
     
    If your skills and experience do not align perfectly with this role, yet you believe you have something unique to offer, we're keen to listen. Reach out to us with a short statement on how you can contribute and let's discuss where you might fit into our team.

raw.description:
About Level Zero
Level Zero is pioneering next-generation biosensor technology for precise, real-time monitoring of critical endocrine biomarkers. Recognised as one of the top 20 startups across all categories worldwide at TechCrunch Disrupt 2024 - and backed by top-tier organisations like SOSV and Entrepreneur First - we’re pushing the boundaries of biochemistry and nanotechnology to revolutionize personalised health.

To achieve this ambitious vision, we’re assembling the best team in the world - dedicated to turning cutting-edge science into life-changing, real-world solutions.
 

About the Role

We are seeking a lead biosensor scientist to drive the development and commercialisation of our continuous aptamer sensor platform. The ideal candidate will have proven expertise in developing continuous monitoring devices for regulated healthcare applications, demonstrated experience transitioning research-stage sensors into manufacturing-ready products, and a track record working with in vivo validation studies and large-scale analytical verification programs.

This is a full-time, in-person role primarily based in London.


What you'll do
  • Lead the development and optimisation of electrochemical continuous sensor systems from bench concept through manufacturing readiness.
  • Design and execute large-scale analytical verification studies, including multi-parameter performance characterisation, stability assessments, and biocompatibility validation.
  • Oversee in vivo validation studies in human subjects and troubleshoot sensor performance in clinical settings.
  • Define manufacturing processes, material specifications, and quality control parameters aligned with regulatory expectations and QMS frameworks.
  • Engage directly with regulatory pathways (FDA, EMA) to define performance specifications and shape submission strategy.
  • Lead cross-functional efforts with electrochemistry, microfabrication, and manufacturing to translate designs into scalable production.
  • Develop technical documentation packages (CMC, analytical performance dossiers) for regulatory submissions and investor communications.
  • Mentor junior scientists and technicians in sensor characterisation and assay validation methodologies.

    • What You Bring
  • A Ph.D. degree in electrochemistry, materials science, biomedical engineering, or related discipline, with specific focus on electrochemical biosensors. Minimum 4 years of industry experience commercialising continuous monitoring or diagnostic sensor technologies.

    • The ideal candidate will possess expertise in the following areas:

  • Deep experience in electrochemical sensor development-particularly amperometric, potentiometric, or impedance-based platforms-with demonstrated progression from research concept to clinical or commercial application.
  • Proven track record managing regulatory submissions (FDA 510(k), De Novo, or CE marking) for continuous monitoring devices.
  • Strong experience designing and executing large-scale analytical verification studies including stability, accuracy, precision, and matrix interference assessments.
  • Demonstrated experience working with in vivo validation studies, including study design, data interpretation, and regulatory reporting.
  • Knowledge of manufacturing readiness, scale-up strategy, and GMP-compatible processes.
  • Proven ability to operate in QMS-ready environments with familiarity of ISO 13485, design controls, and regulatory compliance frameworks.
  • Understanding of biocompatibility, sterility, and shelf-life requirements for implantable or skin-worn continuous devices.
  • Proficiency in surface chemistry, material selection, and biointerface optimisation.
  • Expertise in aptamer-based biorecognition elements and aptamer optimisation for continuous monitoring applications.

    • Nice to have:

  • Experience with microneedle or transdermal ISF technologies.
  • Familiarity with SELEX or aptamer discovery workflows.
  • Experience with MEMS & electrode microfabrication processes.

raw.title: Senior Account Manager (French-speaking)
raw.description:
Who are we

At Lokalise, we make it easy and profitable for businesses to expand into new markets. Our AI-powered localization platform helps companies manage both software and marketing content from a single, unified environment — ensuring every team speaks with one voice across every language and channel.

By automating workflows, integrating with over 60 tools, and centralizing translation memory and terminology, Lokalise enables product, engineering, and marketing teams to collaborate without friction and launch globally up to 10× faster and at 80% lower cost.

Trusted by thousands of businesses across more than 100 countries, Lokalise empowers millions of people worldwide to use digital services in their native languages. Backed by a customer-loved support team, our platform fits seamlessly into your design, development, and content workflows, helping you scale with consistency and control.

Location

While our company operates exclusively on a remote basis, you must reside and have the legal right to work in one of the following countries: the United Kingdom, Latvia, or Spain.

This is a full-time, remote position. Please note that we do not engage on a B2B or contractor basis. We do not partner with search firms.

 

About the Team

We are looking for a Senior Account Manager to join our EMEA team, which focuses on strengthening relationships with existing customers and driving sustainable revenue growth through retention, expansion, upselling, and cross-selling.

In this role, you will own the commercial outcomes and full commercial lifecycle of your assigned enterprise accounts. This includes protecting customer retention, supporting successful renewals, identifying expansion opportunities, and ensuring customers continue to realise value from Lokalise over time.

You will manage a portfolio of strategic customers, with a particular focus on French-speaking stakeholders and organisations. You will act as a trusted commercial partner, helping customers connect Lokalise's capabilities to their business objectives, localisation workflows, and international growth plans.

You will report to the Director of Sales EMEA and work closely with Customer Success, Solutions Architecture, Product, Finance, and Legal. You will be measured primarily on account expansion through upselling, cross-selling, and broader customer adoption and gross revenue retention across your portfolio .

 

What You Will Do

  • Own account commercial outcomes: Take responsibility for the full commercial lifecycle of your assigned enterprise accounts, including retention, renewals, expansion, upselling, and cross-selling.
  • Protect retention and renewal outcomes: Monitor account health, customer engagement, product value, and commercial risks to identify potential retention challenges early and coordinate effective action with internal teams.
  • Drive account expansion: Identify and execute upsell, cross-sell, and expansion opportunities, leading commercial conversations and negotiations with a focus on achieving and surpassing sales quotas.
  • Develop account strategies: Create and maintain clear account plans based on customer goals, stakeholder priorities, product adoption, business risks, renewal plans, and opportunities for broader collaboration.
  • Lead consultative customer conversations: Advise customers on how to improve their localisation and content workflows, connect their needs to Lokalise's solutions, and articulate clear business value and return on investment.
  • Navigate complex enterprise sales processes: Coordinate multi-stakeholder opportunities, procurement activity, contract negotiations, and legal discussions, ensuring progress toward successful commercial outcomes.
  • Partner cross-functionally and maintain accurate reporting: Work closely with Customer Success and Solutions Architecture to support retention and expansion, collaborate with Product, Finance, and Legal to resolve customer needs, and maintain accurate CRM records, account plans, pipeline updates, and forecasts.
  • Use AI to elevate your work: Proactively explore and apply AI tools and approaches to improve customer research, account planning, decision-making, productivity, and go-to-market impact.

 

What You Must Have

  • Full account lifecycle ownership: +5 years of experience owning the commercial lifecycle of strategic or enterprise customer accounts, including retention, renewals, expansion, upselling, and cross-selling in a quota-based B2B SaaS environment.
  • Proven commercial outcomes: A track record of protecting customer revenue, achieving gross revenue retention or comparable retention targets, and generating measurable account expansion.
  • Professional fluency in French, including the ability to lead customer conversations, presentations, and commercial negotiations in French.
  • Ability to understand complex SaaS products, with experience selling to business, marketing, and sales stakeholders, and translating product capabilities into clear commercial value.
  • Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to collaborate effectively across a remote, international organisation.
  • Experience engaging and influencing C-level and senior stakeholders, including the ability to lead strategic conversations and align solutions with business priorities.
  • Strong commercial skills, including experience identifying growth opportunities, negotiating contracts, and navigating complex procurement or legal discussions.
  • Competency using AI tools to accelerate customer research, synthesis, account planning, and decision-making, with a proactive mindset toward adopting new AI-enabled ways of working.

It's a Plus If You Have

  • Experience managing or selling to enterprise customers in the French market, regardless of where you are based.
  • Experience engaging technical stakeholders (e.g., IT, engineering, product) in addition to business buyers.
  • Experience selling localisation, translation management, or other workflow software.
  • Experience working with procurement processes such as RFPs, security reviews, or complex enterprise buying committees.
  • Familiarity with structured sales methodologies or account planning frameworks.

Our Benefits

💰 Competitive salary and employee stock options.

🌍 Fully remote setup with flexible working hours.

🏢 Co-working budget for those days you want a change from your home office.

🌴 Flexible vacation policy to recharge when you need to.

🖥️ Home office setup budget: monitor, desk, ergonomics, whatever helps you do your best work.

📚 Learning & development budget to grow your skills and career.

About Us

Lupa is building a category defining product the industry has never seen before.

We are the AI-native operating system for veterinary practices and pet parents, replacing the fragmented, clunky systems vets have tolerated for years with a single intelligent platform for scheduling, client communication, clinical documentation, and AI-driven care guidance. The traction speaks for itself: one of Europe's top 100 AI startups with a team of 70 people, 10x growth in twelve months, the UK market leader, and now charging hard into the US and Europe. We have $25M in funding, 2.5M+ pets on the platform, and a buzzing HQ in Paddington, London.

This is a rare chance to join a rocket ship at exactly the right moment and we are looking for exceptional people to help us fly it.

In this role, you will:

  • Be Lupa's first in-house legal hire, building the legal function from scratch and owning everything from commercial contracts to regulatory compliance across multiple jurisdictions

  • Own and negotiate all commercial agreements including enterprise SaaS contracts, partner deals, vendor agreements, and everything in between, moving at the pace the business demands

  • Lead data privacy and security compliance across UK GDPR, EU GDPR, and US state privacy laws as we expand internationally

  • Navigate the regulatory landscape for AI-powered clinical tools in veterinary and adjacent healthcare markets across the UK, EU, and US

  • Support the board and leadership on corporate governance, equity matters, and future fundraising processes

  • Manage employment law across an increasingly international team including UK, US, and other jurisdictions as we scale

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure our AI features are built and deployed compliantly, from data handling to clinical liability

  • Own IP strategy, protecting what we build and making sure we are not infringing on what others have built

  • Build relationships with external counsel and manage those relationships commercially and strategically

Your background looks something like:

  • Qualified solicitor or barrister with 7+ years PQE. English and Welsh qualification essential, US bar admission a strong advantage

  • Significant experience in technology, SaaS, or digital health law, ideally with in-house experience at a high-growth startup or scale-up

  • Deep knowledge of data privacy law including UK/EU GDPR and experience operationalising compliance in a product-led company

  • Commercial contract experience at pace. You have negotiated complex enterprise deals and know how to move quickly without creating unnecessary risk

  • Exposure to regulatory frameworks for AI or health tech products (nice to have)

  • Experience supporting a fundraising process at Series A, B, or beyond (nice to have)

  • Background at a top-tier law firm before moving in-house (nice to have)

As a person, you:

  • Are a pragmatic, commercially minded lawyer. Your job is to help the business move fast safely, not to find reasons to slow things down

  • Are comfortable being the only lawyer in the room and making confident calls with incomplete information

  • Build trust quickly across a business, from engineers who need a quick data handling answer to the CEO who needs a board-ready governance opinion

  • Are genuinely excited by the intersection of AI, health tech, and regulation. This space is moving fast and you want to be at the front of it

  • Are excited to work in-person from our Paddington, London HQ

  • Value working with people who are kind, ambitious, and pragmatic

What does success look like in 6 months?

  • The legal function exists. Contracts are standardised, compliance frameworks are in place, and the business is no longer making it up as it goes

  • You are a trusted voice at the leadership table, pulled into strategic decisions early rather than brought in to review at the end

  • The US expansion has legal infrastructure behind it. Entity structure, contracts, employment, and privacy are all covered

Software Engineer, Inference
raw.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the role

The Inference team builds and runs the systems that serve Mistral's models to the world.

We own the path from a trained model to a response on someone's screen. That includes the APIs and gateway that requests come through, routing and scheduling across our GPU fleet, and the capacity, deployment and operations work that keeps it all running.

Our work serves two groups. Customers need fast, reliable and cost-efficient inference as usage keeps growing. Our researchers rely on the same systems for evaluation, data generation and reinforcement learning, so what we build feeds directly into the next generation of models.

 

What You Will Do

As an Engineer on Inference, you'll build and run the services that sit between our users and our models. The work is close to the product and to the hardware, and the improvements you make show up quickly in latency, reliability, cost and how fast we can ship new models.

Experience with LLM inference is a plus, but it isn't a requirement. We're just as interested in strong Systems Engineers from other backgrounds who are keen to go deep on serving.

A few of the problems our teams work on:

  • Designing and evolving our inference APIs, so model capabilities like tool calling, structured outputs and new modalities are available to developers on launch day.

  • The backend services and gateway every request passes through, from authentication, streaming and rate limiting to usage metering, observability and end-to-end reliability.

  • Routing, load balancing and autoscaling across our clusters, so we absorb traffic spikes without wasting GPUs.

  • Faster, safer rollouts of new models and serving releases.

What We're Looking For

  • Have several years of experience shipping and running backend or distributed systems that serve real production traffic.

  • Write high-quality production code, and are comfortable using AI coding tools without compromising on it.

  • Care about performance and reliability, and enjoy making systems faster, cheaper and more robust.

  • Have led the design of significant systems, making the right trade-offs and seeing them through to production.

  • Raise the bar for the engineers around you through code review, design discussions and mentoring.

  • It’s a plus if you’ve shipped production backend services in Python or Go, or operated Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure at scale

  • Experience with LLM serving engines such as vLLM is a strong plus.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

raw.title: Assistant Controller
raw.description:
About MUBI

MUBI is a global streaming service, production company and film distributor dedicated to elevating great cinema. To make this possible, we create, curate, acquire and champion visionary films, bringing them to audiences all over the world. We have a team of brilliant, dedicated and passionate people to help bring our mission to life. From London to New York, Istanbul to Paris, and Berlin to Mexico - we work together to realize MUBI’s vision.

That’s where you come in! Join our global team and help us make great cinema accessible to everyone, everywhere.

About the Role

MUBI is looking for an Assistant Controller to lead our group accounting and financial reporting function from London. Reporting to the Global Controller, you will own the US GAAP close and consolidation, lead group financial reporting and the day-to-day delivery of our Big Four group audit, and oversee statutory accounting across our international entities.

You will directly manage our senior statutory accounting leads. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will stay close enough to the detail to resolve issues and set a high bar for accuracy, while also developing the team, strengthening controls and improving how we close, report and operate.

Your initial mandate is focused on group and statutory accounting. Cash and treasury operations and payroll will initially remain outside your remit. Once the core accounting mandate is firmly established, we expect the role to broaden over time to include greater oversight of cash and treasury. We are therefore looking for someone who already brings meaningful experience in these areas.

You will work closely with the Global Controller on complex accounting matters, systems and automation, controls and the continued development of the function. MUBI's accounting environment spans subscription streaming, film distribution and production across multiple entities, countries and currencies. We are looking for someone who learned the fundamentals in Big Four audit and has since applied them in-house, with the judgement and experience to operate effectively across this complexity as the business continues to grow.

We work hybrid-remote where we require 3 office days in London. Our core days are Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday, with the flexibility to use our offices on the remaining two days if you wish.

Where you’ll have impact:

  • Own the close and consolidation. Lead the month-, quarter- and year-end close and consolidation process across all entities, including review of journal entries, accruals, reconciliations, eliminations and other key close outputs.

  • Lead financial reporting. Prepare and review consolidated US GAAP financial statements, management reporting packs and supporting schedules, ensuring group reporting is accurate, timely and well supported.

  • Own key accounting areas. Oversee accounting for content assets, subscription and distribution revenue, deferred revenue, partner and app-store settlements, intercompany balances and foreign currency. Work with FP&A, content and other teams where accounting depends on operational data or business context.

  • Oversee global statutory accounting. Directly manage our senior statutory accounting leads and coordinate statutory reporting across the group, working with local teams and external advisers to ensure statutory accounts and filings are complete, accurate and delivered on time.

  • Lead the audit. Manage the day-to-day delivery of the Big Four group audit and coordinate statutory audits across our entities. Build an effective relationship with our auditors and advisers and ensure requests and deliverables are well supported and resolved promptly.

  • Strengthen controls and processes. Document and improve accounting processes and SOPs, strengthen key close and reporting controls, and help develop the control environment toward public-company and SOX standards.

  • Partner on technical accounting. Work with the Global Controller and external advisers on new or complex accounting matters, helping translate technical conclusions into clear accounting policies and treatment.

  • Improve systems and automation. Lead improvements to our accounting systems, close and reporting workflows. Use automation and AI where they can materially improve accuracy, speed and efficiency.

What you’ll bring:

  • Active US CPA licence. You hold an active US CPA licence and bring strong practical knowledge of US GAAP.

  • Big Four and in-house experience. You have at least eight years of accounting experience, including meaningful Big Four audit experience and at least two years in an in-house accounting role, ideally within a complex, multi-entity international business.

  • Close and consolidation expertise. You have owned or played a senior role in month-, quarter- and year-end close and group consolidation, including the preparation or review of financial statements, with a strong understanding of the GL and end-to-end financial reporting process.

  • Strong people leadership. You have at least three years of experience managing and developing accounting professionals and are comfortable leading experienced team members across different countries and areas of responsibility.

  • Audit and controls experience. You have acted as a senior company-side contact for external auditors and have experience documenting, operating and improving internal financial controls.

  • International statutory experience. You have overseen statutory accounting and reporting across multiple jurisdictions and know how to work effectively with local finance teams, advisers and auditors without needing to be the technical expert in every market.

  • Meaningful cash and treasury experience. You have practical experience with the core disciplines of cash and treasury in a multi-entity business, including cash reporting or forecasting, banking operations, payment controls and bank reconciliations.

  • Strong systems and process capability. You have experience with NetSuite, Ramp and other finance and accounting systems, plus advanced Excel skills.

  • Clear judgement and communication. You have strong attention to detail, can move comfortably between accounting detail and the wider business context, communicate clearly with senior stakeholders, and manage competing priorities under tight deadlines.

  • You have the right to work in the UK and are able to work in person from our London office.

We want to make cinema accessible to everyone. We believe people from different backgrounds bring different ideas that foster innovation and engagement, allowing us to attract great people to develop the best experience for our users.

MUBI is committed to being an Equal Opportunity Employer. That means it's our responsibility to ensure that all candidates are not discriminated against in our hiring processes and our employment decisions based on their race, color, religion, nationality or ethnic origin, age, gender identity or expression, sex, marital status, physical or mental disability, socioeconomic background, sexual orientation, family or parental status, or any other applicable characteristic.

raw.title: Area Medical Lead, North & Midlands
raw.description:
Mission

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

You own the clinical bar across the Neko clinics in the North and Midlands (currently Birmingham and Manchester).

That means every consultation in your area meets the same threshold of safety, quality, and member experience across your region. It means the clinical teams working with you are developing, not just performing. It means clinical issues are being seen and addressed before they show up in audits or member complaints. And it means the quality metrics for your region are known, owned and moving in the right direction. And it means clinical judgment shows up at the table when operational decisions are being made.

You'll partner closely with the UK Medical Director, who holds final clinical authority for the UK market, and operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager for your region who owns the operational side. The clinical health of the region is yours.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Hold the clinical standard across every site in your area

  • Manage and develop the clinicians in your region: performance conversations, development plans, coaching, and the honest feedback that turns good clinicians into great ones.

  • Ensure lead clinicians in your market(s) are performing excellently and that the clinical teams have the appropriate clinical escalation pathways in place.

  • Support clinical hiring for your area against defined criteria, and partner with the Training and Education team to close training gaps as they emerge.

  • Own the review and closure of clinical incidents and near-misses in your area, making sure learnings are actually applied, not just documented.

  • Own the quality metrics for your region: accountable for performance against Neko's medical quality goals at area level, including scan quality (perfect scan score), member follow-up quality and timeliness (perfect follow-up score and follow-up SLAs), clinical safety (Northstar Clinical Safety score) and clinician summary quality and timeliness. Review the data with your Area Clinic Manager each week and month, trace variation to root cause by site and clinician, set improvement actions, and report progress and risks to the UK Medical Director.

  • Operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager: co-owning quality, member experience, and business goals, attending and contributing to Weekly and Monthly Business Reviews, and bringing clinical input into operational decisions before they're made.

  • Round your sites regularly to observe, support, and listen, surfacing what's working so it can spread, and what isn't so it can be addressed.

  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with the GPs, NHS trusts and private specialist clinicians who receive Neko referrals, monitoring referral quality and addressing breakdowns quickly.

  • Know the UK regulatory landscape: CQC registration and inspection standards, GMC/NMC professional standards and revalidation, NHS and GP referral pathways and obligations, and UK-specific clinical rules, and flag emerging risks before they become problems.

  • Lead or participate in clinical pilots as required - defining success, capturing learnings, and documenting outcomes so the rest of the company can learn from your region.

raw.description:
Mission

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

As the Clinic Area Lead, you will be accountable for bringing Neko Health’s operating model, culture, and member first standards to life across an existing portfolio of clinics in Birmingham and Manchester, as well as future clinics outside of London.

This role sits at the intersection of leadership, execution, and local adaptation, ensuring that global ways of working translate into consistently high quality experiences on the ground, while continuing to mature and evolve as we scale.

Reporting to the Country Manager, UK, you will own regional performance end to end, from new site readiness through sustained multi-site operations. You will act as the cultural and operational anchor for Neko Health in Birmingham and Manchester, setting expectations, building capability, and reinforcing how clinics lead, operate, and serve members.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Continue embedding Neko Health’s operating model across the Birmingham and Manchester clinics, focusing on strong leadership behaviours, cultural norms, and consistent execution rather than net-new process design. Ensure global standards are understood, embraced and brought to life in day-to-day clinic operations.

  • Lead the successful local adoption of existing playbooks and standards, tailoring them thoughtfully to local regulations, team dynamics, and member expectations while preserving the integrity of Neko’s global member experience.

  • Create strong clinic level leadership capability by coaching managers and clinical leads on how to translate standards into practice: setting clear expectations, reinforcing accountability, and role modelling a member first mindset.

  • Establish clear performance rhythms (metrics, reviews, feedback loops) that reinforce behaviours, surface issues early, and continuously improve both team effectiveness and the member experience.

  • Partner closely with the Country Manager, UK and central teams to ensure the global operating model works in practice locally, identifying where light adaptation is required and driving disciplined, high quality implementation at scale.

Clinic & Member Experience

  • Ensure each clinic consistently delivers a seamless, premium member experience aligned with Neko Health's service standards and brand promise.

  • Lead regional initiatives to elevate service quality based on member feedback, NPS insights, and frontline observations, iterating playbooks in real time as you learn.

  • Foster a hospitality-driven culture where empathy, professionalism, and precision define every member interaction, and where that culture is embedded through training, not just expectation.

  • Oversee the physical and experiential standards of all clinics, ensuring consistency in ambiance, cleanliness, and overall presentation across a growing portfolio.

Medical Quality & Compliance

  • Partner with Clinic Leads and Quality team to build and uphold Neko's clinical quality standards in the UK context, ensuring adherence to regulatory requirements from the ground up.

  • Drive continuous improvement in medical delivery and inspection readiness across all sites, establishing audit-ready documentation and escalation protocols.

  • Serve as the bridge between clinic operations and the Medical Excellence team, ensuring best practices are embedded regionally through structured processes rather than informal norms.

Operational & Financial Performance

  • Own regional operational KPIs and full P&L accountability, and continue building the financial frameworks alongside the clinics themselves.

  • Oversee workforce planning and staffing models in collaboration with central teams, building hiring profiles, ramp plans, and scheduling logic suited to Birmingham and Manchester’s demand patterns.

  • Contribute to regional business strategy, including network optimisation, market expansion planning, and new clinic launches.

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Recruit, onboard, lead, and coach a team of Clinic Leads and Lead Operators across all assigned clinics.

  • Build a strong culture of accountability, communication, and collaboration across distributed teams from day one, establishing the norms and rituals that will define how the Birmingham and Manchester team works.

  • Act as the primary regional liaison between clinic teams and central functions, including Customer Support, Facilities, Workforce Planning, People Operations, Talent Acquisition, and Demand Planning.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Proven experience in a senior operational leadership role (Area Director, Regional Director, District Leader, General Manager or equivalent) within a premium, consumer facing, multi-site environment such as premium healthcare adjacent, wellness, fitness or technology enabled services with physical operations/stores.

  • Demonstrated success implementing and embedding established operating models, standards, and playbooks across multiple locations, driving adoption through leadership, coaching, and accountability rather than documentation alone.

  • Strong track record leading clinic level or site level leaders, with the ability to build capability, reinforce culture, and translate standards into consistent day to day execution.

  • Proven financial and operational acumen, including ownership of regional KPIs, budgets, and P&L performance in a scaling context.

  • Ability to balance strategic perspective with hands on execution, particularly during periods of growth, new site openings, and organisational change.

  • Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with confidence operating in a matrixed, fast moving organisation across central and regional teams.

  • Comfort leading through ambiguity and change, with a bias toward action, continuous improvement, and disciplined execution.

  • Ability to be based onsite in Birmingham and Manchester clinics 4 days a week, including regular travel between Manchester and Birmingham as well as any future clinic locations across the UK that are added to your remit.

raw.title: Marketing Associate
raw.description:
Company

Neuphonic is building the future of on-device voice AI.

We develop ultra-low-latency neural text-to-speech systems that enable super-realistic, human-like speech directly on devices. Our focus is on building efficient generative audio models and infrastructure that can run on CPU-constrained hardware, enabling real-time voice interaction without relying on large cloud infrastructure.

By dramatically reducing latency and compute requirements, we are making natural conversational AI possible on phones, embedded devices, browsers, and edge systems. This requires building high-performance systems that bridge machine learning, real-time audio processing, and distributed infrastructure.

Neuphonic was founded in April 2024 and is backed by leading B2B venture capital firms in Europe. Our customers include OEM handset manufacturers, chip manufacturers, and consumer AI companies building the next generation of voice-enabled products.

Our vision is a world where voice becomes the most natural interface for AI, enabling seamless, intuitive interactions that are accessible to everyone.

We’re solving challenging problems across real-time machine learning, edge inference, streaming systems, and ultra-low-latency infrastructure. If you enjoy working in a fast-moving environment and turning technical ideas into something people want to talk about, you’ll feel at home here.

Role

We’re looking for a Marketing Associate to help build Neuphonic’s brand and grow awareness of our technology.

This is a hands-on role for someone early in their marketing career who is excited about AI, startups and technology. You’ll work closely with the founder and wider team across content, campaigns, product launches, events and day-to-day marketing.

We’re looking for someone who is proactive, creative and highly organised. You don’t need to come in with a fully formed marketing playbook. What matters more is that you are curious, move quickly, have good judgement and are happy to take an idea and make it happen.

Your work will include:

  • Creating and publishing content across LinkedIn, X, our website and other relevant channels

  • Helping plan and execute product launches, open-source releases and company announcements

  • Turning technical work from our engineering and research teams into clear, engaging content

  • Coming up with creative ideas to increase awareness of Neuphonic and our products

  • Supporting campaigns across different channels and audiences

  • Helping organise events, demos, conferences and other marketing activities

  • Writing blog posts, case studies, newsletters and other marketing materials

  • Helping keep our website, social channels and marketing materials up to date

  • Tracking the performance of content and campaigns and learning what works

  • Jumping into ad hoc projects and helping wherever needed as the company grows

This is a broad role with lots of opportunity to learn. Some weeks you might be helping launch a new model, others you might be creating content from a research paper, organising an event or testing a new campaign.

You have

  • Around 1–4 years of experience in marketing, content, growth, communications or a similar role

  • Strong written communication skills and the ability to explain ideas clearly and simply

  • A genuine interest in AI, technology and startups

  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail

  • The ability to take ownership of a task and see it through to completion

  • A creative mindset and lots of ideas for how to make technical products interesting

  • A willingness to learn quickly and get involved across different areas

  • Comfort working in a fast-moving environment where priorities can change

In addition, one or more of the following would be particularly valuable:

  • Experience working at a startup or in a small, fast-moving team

  • Experience creating content for a technology or startup audience

  • Familiarity with LinkedIn, X, newsletters or other content channels

  • Experience with tools such as Figma, Canva, Webflow, Framer or similar

  • An interest in developer marketing, open source or technical communities

  • Experience helping with events, launches or campaigns

  • Basic understanding of analytics and measuring marketing performance

Most importantly, we’re looking for a do-er. Someone who is happy to get stuck in, try things and take ownership of getting good work out into the world.

Location: London (King’s Cross)

Benefits

  • Help us set the company culture - you’d be joining us as part of our founding team. Help us set and guide the company culture! Whether it’s breakfasts, reading groups or games nights. Give us your ideas and we’ll make it happen together.

  • Competitive salary and equity - we want to make sure you’re rewarded not just in financial terms but also have a sizeable stake in the business as well. We’re in this together.

  • Private health insurance - your health and well-being is paramount. We want to make sure that everyone in the company is supported when it comes to health.

  • Conference, travel and development budget - your development will also grow the business. We want to make sure that you have access to the resources and opportunities you need to be at your best.

raw.title: Senior People Partner
raw.description:
Who We Are:
Omaze lets people in the UK and Germany win luxury homes and other life-changing prizes while raising money for the causes they love. Our community has raised over £150 million for UK charities in five years, including Age UK, the RSPCA, British Heart Foundation and Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity.

🔑 About The Job

We are hiring a Senior People Partner to help our managers lead well. You will focus on leadership capability, how teams run, and programmes that measurably improve culture and performance. Within a year, our managers should set clearer expectations, handle underperformance earlier and need you less for what they can now do themselves.

You will partner with our managers and senior managers and report to our VP People. We’re a small team, so you will own your work from diagnosis through to adoption.

💪 What you will have done in 12 months

  • Manager capability you can see in the numbers. Managers set expectations, give feedback and address underperformance with confidence, and you can show the before and after.

  • A real team problem fixed. You diagnosed an issue in structure, accountability or decision-making with the leader who owned it, and measured whether the fix worked.

  • A change landed well. Leaders had a clear plan, people understood what was happening and why, and those affected had real support.

  • A programme taken through to adoption. You owned it from diagnosis to rollout, and you reported honestly on whether it made a difference.

🫵 What you will do

  • Coach and challenge managers. Build their confidence and capability in setting expectations, giving feedback, developing talent and addressing underperformance.

  • Improve how teams work. Partner with leaders on team structure, capability, accountability and decision-making.

  • Deliver people programmes. Diagnose the business need, propose practical solutions and own delivery through to adoption.

  • Lead people change. Help leaders plan and implement organisational change, with clear communication and support for the people affected.

  • Give sound advice on sensitive people matters. Bring empathy, commercial judgement and the confidence to challenge.

  • Use AI well. Apply it in your own work and help managers do the same, with sound judgement on confidentiality and accuracy.

🎯 Who this is for

Experienced people partners who coach, diagnose and finish what they start. You have worked in an organisation of 300 or more people, or helped a smaller one grow through that size, so you know what good looks like at scale and when not to apply it.

  • You have designed and delivered a people programme yourself and can show what changed, for example in manager effectiveness, engagement, regretted attrition or time to productivity.

  • You coach managers well, and you can give examples of managers who became more effective and more independent because of you.

  • You connect people issues to business priorities. You use data and employee insight to find causes, and you check whether your fix worked.

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity, you prioritise hard, and you carry work through to completion in a lean team.

  • You use AI in your daily work and can describe exactly how it has changed what you do. You also help others raise their own use, with good judgement on confidentiality and accuracy.

  • You can tell us what you do differently now compared with 18 months ago, and why.

😢 Who this is not for

If your strength is policy administration, process ownership or running People Operations, this is not the right fit, because that work is covered elsewhere. If you want a large HR team to deliver through, you should also know this is a lean team and you will do much of the work yourself.

Useful but not required

CIPD qualification. Experience in a growing business.

🙌 What’s In It For You

  • Generous stock options scheme

  • 25 days annual leave PLUS Bank Holidays

  • Private medical and dental insurance

  • 9% employer pension contributions, when you contribute at least 2%

  • A generous personal learning and development budget each year to use on training courses, conferences and professional memberships

  • Enhanced family leave policies

  • Life assurance of 4x your salary

DEI Statement

We actively seek out diversity of thought and experience to drive innovation. We welcome all backgrounds, identities, and perspectives and work hard to ensure that every Omaze employee can bring their authentic self to work at all times.

raw.description:
About the team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with life sciences organizations to deploy production AI systems across scientific and operational workflows. We work at the boundary of customer deployment and core platform development, using early engagements to define repeatable system patterns, evals, and operating standards for life sciences environments.

About the role

We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to lead end-to-end deployments of our models inside life sciences organizations and research institutions, focusing on workflows across discovery, clinical development, submissions, and scientific operations. You will work with customers who are experts in their domains, translating data, infrastructure, and workflow constraints into production systems and helping define how frontier models can be applied in regulated environments.

You will measure success through production adoption, workflow impact, and eval loops that define workflow-specific benchmarks, acceptance criteria, and launch evidence for production use. You’ll work closely with Business, Research, Platform/Product, Engineering, and Security/GRC, using deployment learnings to improve both customer systems and the product and model roadmaps supporting them.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 30% is required.

In this role you will

  • Own deployments from initial scoping through production adoption, including technical decisions, sequencing, and launch readiness.

  • Partner with customers and internal teams to frame problems, define scope, and translate ambiguous workflow needs into system requirements and measurable endpoints.

  • Define launch criteria for regulated contexts, including validation evidence, outcome metrics, and acceptance thresholds tied to production use.

  • Enforce operating standards for auditability, traceability, and inspection readiness in the systems you ship.

  • Design evals that measure model and system quality against workflow-specific scientific benchmarks and acceptance criteria.

  • Use evaluation results, error analysis, and deployment learning to improve model selection, system design, and product feedback.

  • Distill deployment learnings into reference architectures, validation templates, benchmark harnesses, and other technical primitives that can be reused across life sciences environments.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Bring 6+ years of software, ML/AI, or deployment engineering experience with customer-facing ownership in biotech, pharma, clinical research, scientific software, or adjacent technical domains.

  • Have operated as a senior engineer, tech lead, or deployment owner who is trusted to make technical decisions in ambiguous environments.

  • Have owned customer GenAI deployments end-to-end from scoping through production adoption.

  • Have improved deployed systems through eval design, error analysis, and evidence generation that hones acceptance criteria over time.

  • Have delivered AI systems in workflows such as discovery, clinical development, regulatory writing, submissions, or scientific operations where validation strategy, auditability, compliance constraints, and reviewer expectations shaped system design and rollout.

  • Communicate clearly across scientific, clinical, model research, technical, and executive audiences, translating technical tradeoffs into decisions, operating procedures, and measurable outcomes with credibility and a clear point of view.

  • Apply systems thinking and engineering judgment, turning failures, escalations, and audit findings into improved operating standards, validation artifacts, and repeatable deployment patterns.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.
