About the role

We’re entering a once-in-a-company moment: a major step-change in our D2C marketing investment, a full rebrand of the company and product under the Zable brand, and a marketing function being built out at pace under a newly-appointed CMO. This is one of the most exciting marketing builds in UK fintech right now, with the financial strength, customer base, and product depth to back it up.

Finding and signing new affiliate and influencer partners is the core of our growth engine going forward, and we’re building the team to power it. We’re looking for an Affiliate & Influencer Acquisition Executive whose core mission is sourcing brand-new partners — not just managing the ones we already have. Reporting to a Head of Growth Partnerships, you’ll own the full new-partner funnel end-to-end: mapping affiliates and influencers we don’t work with yet, running outbound outreach, and negotiating CPA or fixed-fee deals structured so every partnership delivers measurable, incremental customer acquisition.

This is an acquisition-first partnership seat: you’ll spend as much time prospecting and pitching new affiliates and influencers as you do modelling payback economics. If you think in CPA, fixed-fee and incremental CAC as naturally as you think in relationships, this role is built for you.

What we're looking for:

Essential:

• Proven track record sourcing and closing brand-new affiliate or influencer partnerships from scratch this is a new-business role, not just account management

• 2-3+ years in affiliate marketing, acquisition or performance marketing roles for a consumer brand

• Fluent in core acquisition performance metrics – CPA, fixed-fee, LTV, ROI and blended CAC and confident structuring CPA or fixed-fee deals that guarantee incremental acquisition

• Working knowledge of channel economics: payback period, cohort behaviour, and how partnership spend compares against other acquisition channels

• Direct experience running affiliate and/or influencer partnership end to end, including commercial negotiation (not just relationship management)

• Track record of running activations end-to-end and delivering measurable results

• Strong account / relationship management skills

• Comfortable with the data — channel economics, attribution and ROI

• Highly organised and detail-oriented — you can run multiple activations in parallel

• Strong commercial communicator — you can hold your own with senior partners

• Demonstrable use of AI in your workflow

Desirable:

• Experience in fintech or financial services

• Experience with sport, entertainment, media or large brand sponsorships

• Experience with an affiliate network or tracking platform (e.g. Impact, Awin, CJ, Partnerize, Income access) and reading platform-level reporting unassisted

• Experience building an affiliate or influencer programme from 0 to 1 in a consumer brand

You’re a good fit if you’re:

• An experienced affiliate marketer who has sourced new customer-acquisition channels, not just managed existing ones

• A natural relationship-builder — partners trust you, and so does your team

• Commercially literate first, relationship-led second – you measure success in growth, not vanity

• Data-fluent – you build your own view on what’s working from raw performance data, not just a dashboard summary

• Hands-on and resourceful — you make things happen

• Curious about AI and how it changes the partnerships discipline

What you'll be doing

New Partner Acquisition:

• Proactively map the affiliate and influencer landscape to identify new partners who can drive incremental customer acquisition

• Run outbound outreach and pitch new affiliates and influencers, building and working a pipeline of prospective partners

• Negotiate and close new commercial deals primarily CPA or fixed-fee structured so every new partner is measurably incremental

• Own onboarding and activation of every new partner, from signed deal through to first live campaign

Commercial & Performance:

• Negotiate commercial terms with affiliates, influencers and sponsorship partners —

prioritising CPA and fixed-fee structures that tie partner pay to genuine incremental customer acquisition — and know which model fits each partner

• Own the unit economics of every live partnership: track CAC by channel and partner against LTV, and flag anything trending the wrong way before it becomes a budget problem

• Build and maintain the channel-economics view that lets the team compare partnership spend against other acquisition channels

• Manage affiliate network/platform relationships (tracking, reconciliation, payout accuracy) and be the first port of call when number don’t match

Activation:

• Run sponsorship and partnership activations end-to-end — brief, plan, ship, measure

• Manage the day-to-day with partners: planning, comms, escalations

• Coordinate across creative, growth, lifecycle and legal

Affiliate Management:

• Own the affiliate relationship from first contact — be the trusted operator they call first, from outreach and onboarding through to ongoing management

• Manage budgets and timelines across activations

• Spot opportunities to expand existing partnerships based on their performance data

Performance & Optimisation:

• Track partnership performance against targets — CPA, CAC, LTV, ROI, Rev Share payout

• Build the playbooks and tooling that scale the function, including standard commercial terms by partner type

• Use AI to scale research, brief-writing and reporting

Cross-functional:

• Partner with creative on activation assets

• Partner with finance and legal on contracts and accruals and commission reconciliation

• Report on partnership performance to the Head of Growth Partnerships, with the numbers to back every recommendation

  • The opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

About the role

We're looking for an analytics engineer to contribute to the analytical foundation of the UK Cards team, a growing area of the business.

You’ll work closely with analysts, product teams, backend engineers, and business stakeholders to improve how data is structured, transformed, and consumed across the company.

The role is fundamentally about building a strong analytical foundation: making it easier for teams to move from question to insight quickly, while maintaining high standards around data quality, scalability, and maintainability.

You'll contribute to the modelling layer, help improve how the business work with data, and support the team in keeping our warehouse a reliable, strategic asset for the business.

What you'll be doing

  • Building and improving the data models that support lending decisions, pricing, portfolio analysis, and investor reporting.

  • Championing standards and contributing to the improvement of our analytics engineering culture.

  • Supporting and collaborating with analysts at different technical levels,helping translate requirements into robust pipelines

  • Helping triage and resolve issues that affect the analytics pipeline or reduce trust in downstream datasets, and contributing ideas to improve the efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness of our transformation pipeline over time.

Our modern data stack

You’ll work with a modern analytics stack centred around SQL, Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran and Claude.

What we're looking for

We’re looking for someone with solid analytics engineering fundamentals and the ability to apply them pragmatically in a fast-moving environment and explain tradeoffs to stakeholders with varying technical depth.

  • Strong DBT and SQL is a must

  • Strong data modelling skills and a good understanding of how analytical datasets should be structured for reliability and usability.

  • Strong experience with ELT pipelines and transformation at scale, ideally using dbt.

  • Experience with Snowflake or another modern cloud data warehouse.

  • Proactiveness in raising areas of data workflows that could be improved and suggesting solutions.

  • A collaborative working style and clear communication across technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Comfort using AI tools effectively to move faster, improve quality, and strengthen day-to-day analytical and engineering workflows

Interview process

  1. 15 minute cognitive assessment

  2. Initial chat

  3. 30 minute chat with hiring manager

  4. 60 minute technical interview

  5. 60 minute culture interview

Zable is the fastest growing credit card in the UK and is revolutionising the credit card industry by making financial tools accessible, intuitive, and empowering. Whether they're building their credit score or looking to save money through refinancing or market-leading offers, we help customers meet their spending and borrowing needs sustainably.

We’re looking for an analytical, commercially-minded Associate Director to own our prime lending strategy and help us scale it fast. You'll own how we price, market and grow our prime business, build and lead a high-calibre analytics team, and put the customer at the heart of every decision.

You’ll operate in a fast-paced environment where ideas matter more than hierarchy, and execution beats bureaucracy. Your work will directly shape who we serve, how we grow, and how we deliver sustainable value.

Your impact

  • Own the prime strategy & economics: Set the vision and roadmap for prime, define the KPIs that matter and own the targets for growth, balances and risk-adjusted returns. Track the portfolio at a granular sub-segment level with Credit Risk, and act fast when things move off plan. Relentless drive to grow the product sustainably, with the energy to bring others with you.

  • Drive pricing & promotions: Own APRs, promotional offers (balance transfer, purchase, etc.), cashback, and fees. Use experimentation and scenario modelling to find the right balance of customer value, growth and profitability, with fair value under Consumer Duty built in.

If you're excited by fintech, lending and scaling products in a fast-moving environment, this role offers real ownership, impact and room to grow.

We're hiring a Associate Product Manager to join the product team, and will cover post booking areas including payments, collections, credit limit increases, spend, and the mobile app.

No two weeks look the same. What you'll work on

  • Running experiments across the customer lifecycle, such as how and when we remind people to pay, what gets them to set up autopay, and how we gamify engagement

  • Working with credit risk and data science on how to apply models to new use cases and opportunities

  • Finding cheap, fast ways to test an idea (a manual process, an email, a script) with AI before committing engineering time to it

  • Gathering customer research to get truthful and unbiased reads

  • Building tools and automations with AI that save time for you, the ops team and the wider business

  • Doing whatever it takes to get something live, including the unglamorous parts like unblocking developers, socializing with legal and compliance, or writing the guide for the ops team

Don’t worry if you don’t meet all these criteria. We'd love to talk to any great candidate that is excited, inquisitive, and a go-getter.

  • You're already using AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex in your work or side projects, and you want to see how far they go

  • You're happy to pick up the small jobs, understanding that as a lean product team no job is too unworthy of our attention

  • You like days that look different from each other

  • Bonus: experience in lending, payments, fintech or a fast-growing startup

Keep in mind: you will not be a fit for this role if you're looking for a well-defined backlog to manage, or you'd rather wait until a problem is fully specified before starting on it. Much of what we work on starts as a loose question with multiple options possible.

AI at Lendable

We want to build the most AI-forward financial services company in the world. PMs here make their own dashboards to answer questions that used to need an analyst, build their own agents and workflows to take care of repetitive work, and ship straightforward changes to production themselves. You don't need to be an expert on day one, but we'll expect you to keep pushing what one person can do.

Your team

You'll report to the Senior Product Manager for Customer Management, and work most closely with:

  • A developer and design team split across London and Europe, covering frontend and backend

  • A data science team building models specific to the US business

  • A credit risk team

  • A growth team

  • An operations team

The team spans our London office, remote engineers in Europe, and our office in Arlington, Virginia, near DC, which you'll visit.

Life at Lendable

  • No one here is limited to their lane. If you want to pick up credit analysis, prototype a feature or fix something in ops, you will be supported.

  • Work from home Mondays and Fridays, and be in the office Tuesday to Thursday, with lunches prepared by our top-tier in-house chefs

This is one of the most exciting marketing builds in UK fintech right now, with the financial strength, customer base, and product depth to back it up.

Direct Mail is one of our highest-potential channels and we’re hiring a leader to turn it into a scaled, precise, and defensible growth engine. We’re looking for a Head of Direct Mail to own the channel end-to-end: creative, sends, logistics, offers, and reporting, sourcing the data pipeline and user-data enrichment that let us target the right customer, with the right offer, at the right moment.

You'll lead the channel's dedicated analysts and work with our creative team. Your job is to set the direction: decide who we mail, with what offer and when, commission and challenge the selection and response models, and hold every campaign to CAC and LTV targets.

Standalone direct mail roles with this kind of budget and autonomy are rare. If you've got significant experience in acquisition mail and want to build a channel your own way, at a profitable business with the product range and analytical capabilities to make it work, this is the role.

  • Experience managing suppliers: tendering, negotiating, setting SLAs and keeping several partners to schedule.

  • The ability to run a multi-drop campaign calendar across products, segments, creative, compliance sign-off, production and mail dates.

  • Experience leading analysts and working closely with creative teams.

  • A clear communicator who earns the trust of finance, risk, compliance and data teams.

  • Demonstrable use of AI in your workflow.

Desirable:

  • Experience in acquisition mail in financial services, especially credit cards or loans, including prescreened or pre-approved offers and risk-based targeting.

  • Experience standing up a data pipeline or enrichment stack (first-party + third-party / bureau data)

  • Experience building a channel or function from scratch

  • Background hiring and developing an analytics or design team

  • Acquisition-minded: you're energised by finding new customers, not re-contacting existing ones.

  • Commercially driven: you measure success in incremental LTV and payback, not response rate alone.

  • A first-principles thinker: you argue from data and clean experiments, not received wisdom

  • Organised: you can run several drops across multiple suppliers and still hit mailing deadlines.

  • Energised by greenfield: you’d rather build the engine than tune someone else’s

Strategy and commercials

  • Own the direct mail strategy and set volume, response and payback targets anchored to LTV.

  • Own the channel P&L: forecasting, budget and CAC/LTV discipline.

Data and targeting

  • Source and buy prospect data from bureaus and brokers, and combine it with our first-party data.

  • Plan and run the campaign calendar, from data selection to the mail landing on doormats.

raw.description:
About Zable

Zable (formerly Lendable) is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.

  • Founded in 2014, profitable since 2017, unicorn since 2021

  • The number one issuer of new credit cards and loans in the UK

  • Backed by Balderton Capital and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan

  • Loved by customers & our team with top reviews on Glassdoor and Trustpilot

Zable was founded on the belief that smarter technology is the solution to lower cost, more transparent consumer finance. Our proprietary foundation models analyse thousands of data points in seconds, drawing a more complete picture of individual financial behaviour. This means we can make better risk decisions, widening access and lowering prices.

The Zable credit card harnesses this technology to deliver better borrowing for three million people. Through our superapp, Zable connects this card to a single platform which makes it effortless to manage credit, get a loan, refinance existing borrowing, switch utilities, get a mobile plan and save more.

Zable is now the number one issuer of new credit cards and personal loans in the UK, but we’ve barely got started. Next, we’re taking our approach to some of the biggest markets in the world - the US and Mexico - where hundreds of millions of people are underserved by outdated bank processes.

Join us if you want to

  • Take ownership across a broad remit - you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Zable from day one

  • Work in small teams of exceptional people - who are relentlessly resourceful to solve problems and find smarter solutions than the status quo

  • Build the best technology in-house - using new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

 

About the role

As Head of Compliance Monitoring, you'll own Zable's risk-based compliance monitoring programme and lead the team that delivers it. You'll provide independent second line assurance that the business meets its legal and regulatory obligations, and evidence the outcomes customers actually receive rather than the processes behind them.

You'll report to the Head of Compliance (SMF 16, Compliance Oversight) and deputise for them, including at Board meetings and sub-committees. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who has built a second line monitoring function in a UK FCA regulated consumer credit firm and wants the autonomy to shape one in a fast-growing fintech. The role is not itself a Senior Manager Function.

What you’ll be doing/impact on objectives

  • Own the compliance monitoring plan and methodology, refreshing it annually and in-year in response to emerging risks, regulatory change, MI, complaints and FCA publications

  • Maintain a monitoring universe covering PRIN and the Consumer Duty, CONC, SYSC, DISP, SMCR, MCOB, the Consumer Credit Act, financial promotions and UK GDPR

  • Scope and deliver thematic and BAU reviews across the customer journey, including affordability (CONC 5), financial promotions (CONC 3), arrears and forbearance (CONC 7), vulnerability, fees and charges and complaints handling (DISP)

  • Test the design and operating effectiveness of first line controls, and provide second line assurance over first line quality assurance

  • Issue clear, evidence-based reports setting out findings, root cause, risk ratings and owned actions, then track remediation to closure and validate that it worked

  • Escalate actual or potential customer harm promptly, and assess it for redress and for notification to the FCA under Principle 11 and SUP 15

  • Produce monitoring MI for the Head of Compliance, executive management and the Board, and present it at committees

  • Support FCA supervisory engagement, information requests and skilled person (s166) reviews, and coordinate coverage with Internal Audit, Risk and first line QA

  • Bring data protection into scope, testing UK GDPR and DPA 2018 compliance alongside the Data Protection Officer

  • Lead, coach and develop the compliance monitoring team, planning resource against the plan and building capability through data, analytics and better tooling

What we’re looking for

  • Demonstrable compliance monitoring experience within a UK FCA regulated firm, including designing, owning and delivering a risk-based compliance monitoring programme

  • Experience of leading, managing and developing a team

  • Consumer credit experience, with a strong working knowledge of CONC and the Consumer Credit Act

  • Strong working knowledge of the FCA Handbook, in particular PRIN and the Consumer Duty, SYSC, DISP and SMCR, and of FCA expectations of a second line monitoring function

  • Data protection knowledge, covering the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018

  • Ability to write clear, concise, evidence-based reports and to present findings credibly to senior management, the Board and its committees

  • Sound judgement and personal resilience, with the independence and confidence to challenge the business constructively and to escalate where necessary

  • Strong planning and organisational skills, with the ability to deliver a plan across competing priorities

Highly desirable

  • Internal audit experience gained in a third line function, and/or a relevant professional qualification (for example IIA, ICA or CISI)

  • Secured lending experience, from either a second or third line perspective, including knowledge of MCOB

 

Interview process

  • Screening stage: a 15 minute remote cognitive exercise and a 30 minute interview with the Talent Partner

  • 40 minute interview with a Compliance Business Partner (remote)

  • Final onsite interview:

    • 45minute interview with the Head of Compliance

    • 30 minute interviews with CRO

    • 30 minute interview with a product MD

We’re entering a once-in-a-company moment: a major step-change in our D2C marketing investment, a full rebrand of the company and product under the Zable brand, and a marketing function being built out at pace. This is one of the most exciting marketing builds in UK fintech right now, with the financial strength, customer base, and product depth to back it up.

Direct Mail is one of our highest-potential channels and we’re hiring a leader to turn it into a scaled, precise, and defensible growth engine. We’re looking for a Head of Direct Mail to own the channel end-to-end: creative, sends, logistics, offers, and reporting, sourcing the data pipeline and user-data enrichment that let us target the right customer, with the right offer, at the right moment.

Standalone direct mail roles with this kind of budget and autonomy are rare. If you've got significant experience in acquisition mail and want to build a channel your own way, at a profitable business with the product range and analytical capabilities to make it work, this is the role.

What we’re looking for:

Essential:

  • 5+ years in direct mail, including at least 2–3 years owning an acquisition DM programme end to end: strategy, budget, data, production and results.

  • A track record of mailing cold prospects at meaningful scale. You'll be able to talk through the volumes, budgets, response rates and CPAs you've been accountable for.

  • Experience procuring data: working with data suppliers on list selection, screening, enrichment and cost.

  • Deep knowledge of the DM supply chain: print, lettershop, Royal Mail products (Advertising Mail, Mailmark, partially addressed, door drops) and suppression (MPS, goneaways, deceased).

  • A strongly commercial approach. You build the business case, forecast volumes and returns, own the channel P&L, and measure spend on CAC, ROI and payback rather than pieces mailed.

  • Strong analytical judgement. You design test cells and holdouts, read results critically, and understand response and propensity modelling well enough to brief analysts, challenge their work and turn it into mailing decisions.

  • Experience managing suppliers: tendering, negotiating, setting SLAs and keeping several partners to schedule.

  • The ability to run a multi-drop campaign calendar across products, segments, creative, compliance sign-off, production and mail dates.

  • Experience leading analysts and working closely with creative teams.

  • A clear communicator who earns the trust of finance, risk, compliance and data teams.

  • Demonstrable use of AI in your workflow.

Desirable:

  • Experience in acquisition mail in financial services, especially credit cards or loans, including prescreened or pre-approved offers and risk-based targeting.

  • Experience standing up a data pipeline or enrichment stack (first-party + third-party / bureau data)

  • Experience building a channel or function from scratch

  • Background hiring and developing an analytics or design team

You’re a good fit if you’re:

  • Acquisition-minded: you're energised by finding new customers, not re-contacting existing ones.

  • Commercially driven: you measure success in incremental LTV and payback, not response rate alone.

  • A first-principles thinker: you argue from data and clean experiments, not received wisdom

  • Organised: you can run several drops across multiple suppliers and still hit mailing deadlines.

  • Energised by greenfield: you’d rather build the engine than tune someone else’s

What you’ll be doing

Strategy and commercials

  • Own the direct mail strategy and set volume, response and payback targets anchored to LTV.

  • Own the channel P&L: forecasting, budget and CAC/LTV discipline.

  • Decide how far and how fast to scale, based on the economics.

Data and targeting

  • Source and buy prospect data from bureaus and brokers, and combine it with our first-party data.

  • Direct the analysts building the response and propensity models that decide who we mail, with what offer and when.

  • Work with risk analysts to shape offers around eligibility and lifetime value.

Campaigns and supplier management

  • Plan and run the campaign calendar, from data selection to the mail landing on doormats.

  • Select, negotiate with and manage print and postal suppliers on cost, quality and turnaround.

  • Brief the creative team on packs, copy and offers, and take them through compliance sign-off.

Reporting & Team

  • Build the reporting that ties sends to funnel, revenue and LTV and report on channel performance

  • Partner with data, product, risk, finance and the creative team to unlock targeting and offers

About the role

This role is for someone wanting to start a career in operations within a financial services firm. You'll join as a Graduate focused on working complaints and train to become a fully competent Complaints Officer, investigating and resolving our more complex customer interactions across loans, cards and auto-finance. A critical role to help the business understand how it can serve customers better.

This is a casework role. From early on you will hold your own caseload, speak to customers directly, make decisions on whether we got it right, and put things right where we didn't. You will be supported through structured training, coaching and quality feedback as you develop in the role

Some of the areas you'll delve into are:

  • The regulatory framework for complaints: FCA regulation, the DISP rules, Consumer Duty, and how the guidance is applied to real cases.

  • Investigation technique: gathering evidence, interrogating system records and call recordings, and testing what actually happened against what should have happened.

  • Decision making and redress: reaching fair and objective outcomes, and calculating and explaining any compensation due.

  • Customer communication: writing final response letters that break complex issues down into plain English.

  • The Financial Ombudsman Service: how cases are referred, how FOS reaches its view, and how we apply those learnings to future cases.

  • Root cause and feedback: spotting the product and process failures behind complaints and feeding them back to frontline and product teams.

Reporting to a Complaints Manager within the Operations Team, you will be responsible for a live caseload and for the quality of the decisions you make on it.

Our ability to handle complaints effectively for our customers and therefore for us as a business has never been more important than now, as we expand our existing products in the UK and US financial markets.

What you'll be doing

  • Investigating and resolving complaints about our loans, cards and auto-finance products, taking each case on its own merits

  • Self-managing a varied and increasingly complex caseload: prioritising cases, choosing the best contact mechanism for each customer, and working efficiently enough to meet our KPI minimum standards

  • Communicating with complainants in writing and by phone — managing expectations, handling difficult situations with tact and professionalism, and finding solutions to the issues raised

  • Writing professional final response letters that set out our decision, our rationale and the customer's right to refer to the Financial Ombudsman Service

  • Following our complaint handling standards and keeping clear records, making sure every decision is backed by demonstrable evidence and a documented rationale

  • Working to resolve complaints without the customer needing to refer to FOS, and applying the learnings from both internal and FOS outcomes to future cases

  • Feeding back to frontline and product teams on the product and process improvements your cases surface, across Operations and the wider business

  • Keeping your knowledge of Zable's products current through effective use and review of our policies, procedures and business tools

  • Turning your hand to other areas of operational need as the business requires

  • An aptitude for investigation, analysis, problem-solving and dispute resolution

In six years, Zable has built a profitable, market-leading credit card in the UK. In 2023, we brought that playbook to the US and set an even higher bar. This year the US credit card business scaled rapidly: our run rate grew more than 20x in the last six months.

A lot of the work of getting customers through the door is in place. The next stage is about what happens once they’re in: helping them pay on time, giving more credit to the ones who earn it, getting people back on track when they fall behind, and ensuring an intuitive user experience across channels.

If you're excited by fintech, lending and scaling products in a fast-moving environment, this role offers real ownership, impact and room to grow.

About the role

We're hiring a Product Manager to join the product team, and will cover post booking areas including payments, collections, credit limit increases, spend, and the mobile app.

No two weeks look the same. One week you might be sizing an opportunity, the next week sitting with the ops team to understand why customers are calling, or putting a rough version of an idea in front of real customers before anyone builds the proper one. We care more about how quickly we learn than how polished the first attempt looks.

What you'll work on

  • Running experiments across the customer lifecycle, such as how and when we remind people to pay, what gets them to set up autopay, and how we gamify engagement

  • Working with credit risk and data science on how to apply models to new use cases and opportunities

  • Finding cheap, fast ways to test an idea (a manual process, an email, a script) with AI before committing engineering time to it

  • Gathering customer research to get truthful and unbiased reads

  • Building tools and automations with AI that save time for you, the ops team and the wider business

  • Doing whatever it takes to get something live, including the unglamorous parts like unblocking developers, socializing with legal and compliance, or writing the guide for the ops team

What we're looking for

Don’t worry if you don’t meet all these criteria. We'd love to talk to any great candidate that is excited, inquisitive, and a go-getter.

  • 1-4 years in product, strategy, analytics, consulting or operations, with some time spent working closely to product or execution teams to deliver value

  • You ask a lot of questions and you're not satisfied until you understand why something is happening

  • You enjoy forming a hypothesis and finding the quickest way to test it, even if the first version is rough

  • You're comfortable with data: you can write SQL or Python and answer your own questions

  • You're already using AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex in your work or side projects, and you want to see how far they go

  • You're happy to pick up the small jobs, understanding that as a lean product team no job is too unworthy of our attention

  • You like days that look different from each other

  • Bonus: experience in lending, payments, fintech or a fast-growing startup

Keep in mind: you will not be a fit for this role if you're looking for a well-defined backlog to manage, or you'd rather wait until a problem is fully specified before starting on it. Much of what we work on starts as a loose question with multiple options possible.

AI at Zable

We want to build the most AI-forward financial services company in the world. PMs here make their own dashboards to answer questions that used to need an analyst, build their own agents and workflows to take care of repetitive work, and ship straightforward changes to production themselves. You don't need to be an expert on day one, but we'll expect you to keep pushing what one person can do.

Your team

You'll report to the Senior Product Manager for Customer Management, and work most closely with:

  • A developer and design team split across London and Europe, covering frontend and backend

  • A data science team building models specific to the US business

  • A credit risk team

  • A growth team

  • An operations team

The team spans our London office, remote engineers in Europe, and our office in Arlington, Virginia, near DC, which you'll visit.

Life at Zable

  • No one here is limited to their lane. If you want to pick up credit analysis, prototype a feature or fix something in ops, you will be supported.

  • Work from home Mondays and Fridays, and be in the office Tuesday to Thursday, with lunches prepared by our top-tier in-house chefs

  • Top-tier private health insurance

  • Offsites for the US Cards product and engineering team, and an annual whole-company trip abroad (previously Turkey and France)

Zable is a high-growth FinTech building its security operations capability deliberately. As a Senior Security Operations Analyst, you will triage and respond to security alerts, help improve the quality of the detections behind them, and lead the response when a security event becomes an incident.

You will investigate alerts and escalations from our MSSP, tune our monitoring so that it finds more of what matters and less of what doesn’t, and act as a trusted Incident Commander for security incidents, from declaration through to post-incident review. You will work with Engineering, IT, Legal, Risk and senior stakeholders, and you will be credible with all of them.

AI is used widely across the business, in how we build software, run operations and serve customers, and that changes both what security incidents look like and how quickly we can respond to them. You will use AI and automation as a normal part of your work, and you will be able to investigate and respond to incidents where AI tooling is the cause, the target or the route in.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone with hands-on SOC experience and a track record of commanding incidents.

1. Alert Triage & Monitoring

  • Triage and investigate alerts across our SIEM, EDR, identity and cloud tooling, taking escalations from our MSSP’s first-line team.

  • Reduce false positives and alert fatigue by tuning detection rules, thresholds and suppressions.

  • Utilise AI and automation to speed up triage, enrichment and response, and to remove repetitive manual work from the analyst workflow.

2. Incident Command & Response

  • Command security incidents, coordinating technical response, decision-making and communications across Engineering, IT, Legal, Risk and senior stakeholders. Give clear, timely updates to executives during live incidents.

  • Lead or support technical investigation and containment across endpoint, identity and cloud (AWS/GCP) environments, including incidents involving AI use, such as prompt injection, or credentials exposed through AI-generated code.

  • Run blameless post-incident reviews, track actions to closure, and feed lessons back into detection, playbooks and controls.

  • Take part in the out-of-hours on-call rota.

3. Operational Reporting & Assurance

  • Track and report SecOps metrics that reflect reality, such as alert quality, time to triage, time to contain, incident volumes and root causes.

  • Maintain accurate incident records and evidence in our incident management platform to support audit and assurance activity.

  • Build working relationships with Engineering, Platform and IT Systems so that incident response is practised before it is needed.

  • Proven incident command: Demonstrable experience leading significant security incidents as Incident Commander or lead responder, from declaration to resolution and review. You can describe incidents you have run, the decisions you made and what you changed afterwards.

  • Technical investigation skills: Solid hands-on SOC/DFIR experience, including log analysis, endpoint and identity investigation, and cloud incident response in AWS or GCP.

  • AI fluency: You understand how AI use creates security risk, including data exposure, agent misuse and AI-assisted attacks, and you can investigate and contain incidents that involve it.

  • AI-first ways of working: You already use AI and automation to speed up your own work, whether in investigation, enrichment, detection engineering or reporting, and you can judge when to trust the output and when to check it.

  • Composure and influence: You stay calm and structured under pressure, and can direct engineers and senior stakeholders without formal authority over them.

  • Communication: You can brief a senior leader in plain language during a live incident, and write a post-incident report that an engineer, an auditor and a board member can each use.

  • Pragmatism: You understand that security supports a business moving quickly, and you balance risk, speed and proportionality in your decisions.

  • Regulated environment awareness (desirable): Experience in financial services or another regulated sector, including incident reporting and evidence expectations.

  • Certifications (desirable, not required): GCIH, GCFA, GCIA, or equivalent practical experience.

Ready to build data platforms, not just pipelines?

At Opencast, we believe great data engineering is about more than moving and transforming data. It's about creating reliable, scalable foundations that help organisations make better decisions and deliver better services.

You’ll tackle complex engineering challenges across integration, migration, modelling and platform design, working with Microsoft Fabric, Azure and modern data technologies. We value engineering craft, thoughtful problem-solving and building solutions that are simple, robust and built to last.

Our data engineering capability is growing, and you'll help guide its direction through mentoring, recruitment and technical leadership, as well as your client work. If you want to shape both the solutions and capability around them, this could be the role for you.

 

The role

  

Opencast data engineers help organisations transform how they manage, use and learn from data. The work ranges from building modern lakehouse and warehouse platforms in Microsoft Fabric to modernising legacy environments, migrating complex workloads and improving the quality, governance and reliability of critical data services.  

 

This role offers the opportunity to work across the full data lifecycle, combining platform design, engineering, integration and optimisation. Expect to work with structured, semi-structured and unstructured data, building batch and near real-time data pipelines that underpin critical business and public services.  

 

You'll collaborate with architects, analysts, software engineers and client teams to solve complex challenges and influence technical direction. The role also offers opportunities to contribute beyond delivery through mentoring, recruitment, community building and helping to define engineering standards and best practice as our capability continues to grow. 

 
 

Requirements

 
This role involves weekly on-site work, and you’ll be required to travel regularly to client locations across the UK. We’re looking for people who value in-person collaboration, enjoy building strong relationships, and are passionate about delivering solutions that make a real difference for our clients.
 
Due to the nature of this role, you must either hold active Security Check (SC) clearance or be eligible and willing to undergo the clearance process. 
 
SC clearance is granted in line with UK Government security vetting requirements. Typically, applicants must have UK citizenship and have lived continuously in the UK for at least the past five years, with no single absence exceeding 28 consecutive days. Nationality and immigration status may also be considered as part of the vetting process. We are unable to progress applications from candidates who do not meet these requirements.
 
If you are unsure whether you meet the eligibility criteria, we encourage you to review the guidance or discuss this with us before applying.
 

We are recruiting for multiple positions, with opportunities available immediately and in the coming months. If you are interested in joining Opencast, we encourage you to apply. 

 
 

Essential experience

 
 
We're looking for engineers who enjoy solving complex technical problems and care about building solutions that are robust, scalable and built to last. 
 
Experience in the following areas is important: 
  • Microsoft Fabric and Azure data services, including lakehouse, warehouse, notebooks and pipeline capabilities.  
  • Building enterprise-scale data platforms, lakehouses and data warehouses.  
  • Data modelling and dimensional modelling techniques such as Kimball. 
  • ETL/ELT development and large-scale data integration.  
  • PySpark, Spark SQL and modern transformation techniques.  
  • Advanced SQL and relational databases including SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Oracle. 
  • Integrating structured, semi-structured and unstructured data sources.  
  • Migration and modernisation of legacy platforms such as Oracle, SQL Server/SSIS or Synapse.  
  • Power BI semantic models, curated datasets and supporting analytics platforms. 
  • Data quality, governance, metadata management and lineage. 
  • Data security, classification and access control approaches. 
  • Automated testing, validation, reconciliation testing and performance optimisation. 
  • DataOps, CI/CD and version control practices.  
  • Agile delivery environments. 
 

Essential consulting skills

 
 

Our clients look to us for more than technical delivery. 

 

Success in this role comes from being able to navigate ambiguity, solve difficult problems and help clients make confident technical decisions. The strongest consultants combine technical expertise with curiosity, pragmatism and a collaborative mindset. 

 

You'll thrive in this role if you enjoy: 

  • Solving complex engineering challenges and exploring different approaches to finding the right solution.  

  • Influencing technical direction through expertise, evidence and constructive challenge.  

  • Working closely with technical and non-technical stakeholders to understand underlying problems rather than simply implement requirements.  

  • Balancing engineering quality, governance, security and reliability with business outcomes.  

  • Sharing knowledge, mentoring others and helping raise engineering standards.  

  • Building trusted relationships with clients and acting as a technical advisor.  

  • Keeping pace with emerging technologies and evaluating new approaches where they can add value.  

  • Contributing to a growing engineering capability while remaining close to delivery and technology. 

 

 

Salary

 
£61,000 - £70,000 per annum.
 

What we offer


A competitive package including a 7% employer pension contribution, share options, and a discretionary bonus. You’ll also benefit from 25 days’ holiday and access to 3 annual “life happens” days to support unexpected situations.  We provide wellbeing support, ongoing professional development, volunteering opportunities, and the chance to be part of a genuinely supportive team.

Where you’ll work


This role requires regular on-site attendance at our HQ, hub offices, and client sites, as well as the ability to work from home. Applicants must be able to travel to offices and client sites across the UK as part of their normal working arrangements, as travel is essential for fulfilling the responsibilities of the role.

We include you


We welcome candidates from all identities, attributes, ways of thinking and backgrounds to thrive in a career at Opencast. Our aim is for the diversity of our people to be reflected in the solutions we deliver, to help create a fairer society for all.   

Interview

raw.title: Senior Compliance Operations Analyst (KYB)
raw.description:
About Plasma

Plasma is building the primary account for global money.

Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.


The Team & Our Story

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.

Plasma is growing fast across international markets, and the businesses we work with need to get onboarded quickly and safely. We're growing the Customer Experience Team to keep up, and this role is fully focused on KYB (Know Your Business).

You'll own the customer side of business onboarding, from the first document request to final approval. While we verify who a business is, who owns it and how it operates, you'll be the person they deal with. Our KYB playbook is still being built, so you won't just follow the process. You'll help write it, set the standards we hold ourselves to and shape the culture of the team as it grows.

This isn't a 9 to 5. You'll need some flexibility on hours and the odd weekend shift to keep coverage strong and handle busy periods. We want someone who works hard, takes ownership without being asked, does well when things move fast and genuinely cares about what we're building.

The role

  • Own the KYB customer experience: Be the main point of contact for businesses going through onboarding. You will handle their queries across chat, email and support tooling, explain what we need and why, and take accountability for the quality and speed of every response.

  • Run KYB reviews end to end: Collect and review company documents such as certificates of incorporation, registers of directors and shareholders, proof of address and ownership structures. Identify ultimate beneficial owners and check that what a business tells us matches what the documents show.

  • Screen and assess risk: Carry out sanctions, PEP and adverse media checks on businesses and their key people, assess the nature of the business and its expected activity, and apply the right level of due diligence based on risk.

  • Know when to escalate: Recognise higher-risk cases, complex ownership structures and red flags, and escalate them to Compliance with a clear, well-documented summary.

  • Build the foundations: Many of our KYB templates, document checklists and customer guides do not exist yet. You will create them, so that customers know what to expect and the team works to one consistent standard.

  • Work across teams: Partner closely with Compliance, Sales and Product so that the business onboarding journey is joined up, compliant and clear for the customer. Flag the most common issues so that our processes can be improved.

    We're a close team and everyone pitches in. When the wider CX team gets busy, we'll count on you to jump in and help out, and they'll do the same for you.


The Bar

  • 3 to 6 years of experience in KYB, onboarding or customer operations, ideally within fintech, payments or crypto. We will consider strong candidates from outside these sectors if the fit is right.

  • Hands-on KYB knowledge. You understand how to verify a company, read corporate documents and work through ownership structures to identify beneficial owners and have good judgement on Risk.

  • High attention to detail. You notice when a name, date or ownership percentage does not line up, and you keep clear records of what you checked and why.

  • Someone who takes ownership & is organised under pressure. You do not wait to be told. When something is broken or missing, you fix it or flag it. You hold yourself to a high standard even when no one is watching.You can manage a queue of open cases, prioritise effectively and keep quality high when things are busy.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity. This is an early-stage company. Processes will change, priorities will shift, and some days you will be figuring things out as you go. You see that as interesting rather than frustrating.

  • Curious about crypto. You need to understand the basics of how stablecoins and digital assets work and be motivated to learn more. Many of the businesses we onboard operate in this space.

Nice to have

  • Experience onboarding crypto businesses, such as exchanges, VASPs, payment providers or OTC desks.

  • Familiarity with AML regulations and frameworks, for example FATF guidance, EU AML directives or FinCEN requirements.

  • Exposure to KYB and screening tools such as Sumsub, ComplyAdvantage, Persona, Middesk or similar.

  • Experience with support tooling like Intercom or Zendesk in a live production environment.

  • Experience in a startup or scale-up where you had to build or rebuild processes, not just follow them.

  • A compliance qualification such as ICA or CAMS, or an interest in working towards one.

  • Multilingual skills that could support business customers across our international markets

What's in it for you

  • Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.

  • A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.

  • Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.

  • Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.

  • All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.

  • Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

We are committed to protecting the privacy and security of your personal data. Any personal information you provide during the recruitment process will be processed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable local data protection laws.

We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

raw.description:
Getting homes off fossil fuels means fitting millions of heat pumps, solar panels and batteries, and every one has to be designed, sold and fitted by an installer. The assets themselves already work brilliantly, but getting them into homes is still slow, complex and painful. Our mission is to change that: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run a renewables installation business, and get homes off fossil fuels way faster.

In just a few years we've become the leading platform for heat pump installers in the UK and Ireland, with around half of all heat pump installations now being managed on Spruce. We've just launched our solar and battery product, and we're building on that to go after even bigger opportunities: every other type of job these installers do, the rest of how they run their business, and a bunch of new countries.

We're now on the hunt for someone truly brilliant to own our socials: making content installers look forward to watching, and turning that attention into customers.

 

🌲 About Spruce

  • Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.

  • We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.

  • We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have doubled the team and grown revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, have just launched an end-to-end solar and battery product, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…

 

🥖 The role

You'll work closely with Hector and the wider growth team. You'll be our first dedicated social hire. Almost nobody is making great content for installers, so the field is wide open and it's yours to build. Your goal is to make Spruce the account every installer follows. Day-to-day you'll be:

  • Making the content yourself – You'll take each piece from idea to script, shoot, edit and post: installer stories, site visits, founder clips, and new out-of-the-box ideas with a real shot at going viral. You'll have the freedom to try anything, and to bring in freelance editors or videographers when that gets better content out sooner.

  • Getting people on camera – You'll spend time on site with our customers and make installers look brilliant on camera. You'll get our own team on camera too, from sales to the devs who build the product.

  • Getting the mix right – You'll balance videos that entertain (skits, challenges, series), teach installers something useful, build trust through real installer stories, and show what Spruce does, so the account never feels like an advert. You'll keep testing new formats, trends and collabs with installer creators.

  • Owning our socials – You'll run Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn and Facebook: the voice, what we make, and what goes out and when. You'll do more of what works and drop what doesn't.

  • Building a community – You'll reply to comments and DMs yourself, and build a community of installers who want to be featured: an audience that becomes our customers.

 

🫵 About you

We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft.

You don't need a particular job title or a set number of years, but you do need to show us something you grew: an account, a channel, a series or a brand. You'll ideally be:

  • A proven creator – you've grown an account, you've had videos that travelled well beyond your normal reach, and you can tell us why they worked;

  • Obsessed with what works – you study what's working on TikTok, Reels and Shorts this week (not last year), you have strong opinions about hooks, and you're always learning what's taking off and what's dying;

  • Properly hands-on – you do most of the shooting and editing yourself and you're quick, and you use AI tools to go faster;

  • Comfortable on camera – you're happy being the talking head yourself, and even happier getting a great take out of an installer who's never been filmed;

  • Curious about the numbers – you check how every post did because you want the next one to be better, not because you love a dashboard;

  • Interested in installers – you see small business owners doing technically complex, physically demanding work, with a brilliant story in every one, and you want to understand their world, not just film it.

Bonus points if you've had videos pass a million views or grown an account to 100k+ followers.

… and you'll hopefully also love heat pumps! 🤓

 

🌟 Our offer

  • 💰 £40–60k salary, depending on experience

  • 🍰 Equity (options) in the company

  • 🏡 Hybrid working: 2–3 days in-person a week (London or Bristol), with full-team meetups every fortnight

  • 🏖️ 33 days holiday (25 plus bank holidays) and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year

  • 🏥 Private Medical Cover (Vitality)

  • 👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme (YellowNest)

  • 🧑‍🍼 Enhanced Parental Leave

  • 🚲 Cycle to Work scheme

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow

 

🧑‍💻 Working at Spruce

  • We're currently a close-knit team of 35, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2–3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone together every fortnight.

  • You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense.

  • We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions.

  • We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it and what we can learn – and never blame. You'll own your outcomes whilst knowing the team has your back.

Thought Machine is building the future of banking. Because our clients are regulated financial institutions, the way we select, manage and oversee our own suppliers matters to them as much as it does to us.

The Risk & Compliance team sits within Finance and is responsible for enterprise risk management, the internal controls framework, regulatory compliance, external certifications (including SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 22301 and PCI DSS), client audits and third-party risk management and procurement. The Supplier & Third Party Risk Manager will take end-to-end ownership of our third-party vendor ecosystem. Using our procurement platform (Omnea), you will lead commercial negotiations, proactively manage contract renewals, and establish a robust Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) programme to safeguard the company against commercial, operational, regulatory and security risk. This is a builder role: we have the tooling and the onboarding process in place, and we are looking for someone to turn it into a mature procurement and supplier management capability that delivers measurable cost savings and better outcomes from our suppliers.

What you will do

Establish and lead the TPRM programme

Proactive renewals management

Strategic sourcing and negotiation

  • Identify consolidation opportunities across enterprise-wide software spend and track savings delivered.

System ownership and process automation

  • Act as the primary business owner for Omnea.

  • Use the platform to automate intake requests, route conditional security risk assessments, track contract approvals, and maintain a centralised repository of active suppliers.

Vendor governance and performance

  • Design and implement a structured vendor governance framework.

  • Segment the supplier portfolio by criticality and establish ongoing monitoring (SLAs / KPIs) for high-risk and critical vendors.

  • Produce regular reporting on supplier performance, risk and spend for senior management.

Business partnership

  • Act as a commercial partner and advisor to department leaders across the business to support their purchasing needs, helping them navigate onboarding smoothly.

What we are looking for

Essential

  • 3–6 years' experience in Procurement, Sourcing or Vendor Risk Management, ideally within a high-growth scaleup, regulated fintech or fast-paced financial services environment.

  • Practical experience running third-party risk assessments, with an understanding of fundamental security and data privacy standards (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2 and GDPR).

  • A track record of managing contract lifecycles, identifying consolidation opportunities, and using usage data to negotiate better renewal terms.

  • Good negotiation skills with a track record of delivering cost savings and driving value from suppliers.

  • A proactive, builder mindset, with the ability to design processes and establish strong internal relationships.

Desirable

  • Familiarity with regulatory expectations on outsourcing and third-party risk in financial services (e.g. DORA, EBA outsourcing guidelines, PRA SS2/21).

raw.description:
About the role

This role exists to make sure everybody at Unity — every Partner and Functional Leader, and everyone in their teams — can actually use AI well in their everyday work, and to turn that capability into real automation and productivity gains across the business. It reports jointly to the Chief People Officer and the Chief AI Officer, because doing this well is as much about people, capability and how Unity actually works day to day as it is about the technology itself.

It suits someone who lives at the frontier of what's possible with AI — building with the latest tools themselves and evolving their own approach every few weeks, not working from a playbook that's a year out of date. It suits someone who gets real satisfaction from building capability in others, reimagining how work actually gets done, and shipping things that stick, rather than setting technology direction from the top. You'll be building the operational muscle of Unity's AI Centre of Excellence from scratch, and sequencing what matters most first.

What you'll own

  • Firm-wide AI capability and training: design and drive practical AI upskilling across client-facing and enablement teams, working closely with the Performance & Development Lead so AI capability is built into onboarding and ongoing development, not run as a separate initiative

  • Reimagining the work: spot where new AI capability means Unity can remove whole steps or approach a problem completely differently, not just automate what already exists, then get alongside client teams and enablement functions to make it real

  • Automation and adoption: identify, prioritise and deliver automation that maximises the value Unity gets from the AI tools already in use, and evaluate new ones on their merits

  • Role and ways-of-working design: as AI takes on more of the work, help Unity rethink who does what, where judgement sits and how junior people learn — including, as whole workflows move onto Weaver, designing the team and role changes that follow: new responsibilities around workflow ownership, supervision, judgement and exceptions

  • Governance in practice: implement the policies and guardrails the Chief AI Officer sets for safe, compliant and ethical AI use — covering data privacy and client confidentiality — making sure they're followed in practice without slowing teams down

  • Build, ship and partner with Engineering: personally build and ship smaller tools and prototypes using the latest AI capabilities; bring in VP Product and Engineering when something needs shared integrations, scaling or ongoing production support

  • Tooling and vendor management: manage the day-to-day AI tooling estate: select, pilot and manage relationships with AI platforms and vendors, and retire what isn't earning its place, working with the enterprise IT team on infrastructure and security

  • Measurement and reporting: build a simple set of KPIs for adoption, automation impact and ROI, and report progress jointly to the Chief People Officer and Chief AI Officer

What success looks like in year one

  • Everybody at Unity, from Partners to enablement staff, confident and capable using AI well in their day-to-day work

  • Several whole steps or processes genuinely reimagined or removed — not just automated — with visible productivity gains across client delivery and enablement functions

  • Every new and existing employee equipped with practical, role-relevant AI skills, not generic training

  • A clear, shared view with the CAIO and CPO of how roles, judgement and team shape need to evolve as more work moves onto AI and platforms like Weaver

  • AI guardrails followed in practice across the business, without becoming a source of friction

What we're looking for

  • Someone who lives at the frontier: actively building with the latest AI tools themselves and evolving their own approach every few weeks. Come with examples of what you've built — we want to see it, not just hear about it

  • A senior operator with a genuine track record of delivering AI and automation adoption at an organisational level — we're more interested in evidence of real impact than where you've done it before

  • A genuine interest in ways of working, role design and how people actually do their jobs, not just the technology — this is a people and change role as much as a technical one

  • Comfortable building smaller things yourself — prototypes, scripts, workflows — and clear-eyed about when to bring in VP Product and Engineering for shared integrations or production-grade build

  • Comfortable building the operational muscle of a function from scratch, and sequencing what matters most first rather than trying to do everything at once

  • Confident training and influencing Partners and Functional Leaders directly, translating strategy into practical, adopted value

  • A pragmatic operator who executes guardrails without adding bureaucracy — in keeping with Unity's "progress over process" and "light scaffolding" principles

  • Excellent communicator, able to make AI capability accessible and credible to non-technical audiences at every level

How this role fits at Unity

You'll report jointly into the Chief People Officer and the Chief AI Officer — a deliberate dual line, reflecting that this role is as much about capability, learning and ways of working as it is about AI itself. You'll work closely with the Performance & Development Lead so AI capability-building lines up with Unity's wider approach to development and growth, and directly with Partners and Functional Leaders across client teams and enablement functions on automation, adoption and reimagining how work gets done.

About Wordsmith

Legal touches everything that matters in a business: every deal, every hire, every launch, every risk. Sales runs on Salesforce. Engineering runs on GitHub. In-house legal runs on inboxes, chat threads and tools that weren’t built for it.
Wordsmith is changing that. We’re building the platform in-house legal runs on.

Requests from across the business come in through one front door. AI agents handle the routine work. Lawyers stay in control where judgment matters. Legal finally gets to triage by risk, not by whoever shouted loudest.

We’re built for in-house teams, not law firms. Our customers want to spend less on outside counsel, not more, and we’re on their side of that equation.

More than 500 companies run on Wordsmith, including Financial Times, Canva, Trip.com, Revolut, Adyen, Trustpilot, and Sage. We’ve raised $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, and we’re growing fast.

Every customer we win deserves a brilliant experience from day one.


About the role

We are hiring an Account Manager to join our existing team and help turn some of the most respected companies in the world into Wordsmith's biggest customers. This is a London-based, quota-carrying role, selling into an existing book of enterprise accounts and working closely alongside the Customer Success Manager. Your focus is growth: cross-selling is your number one priority, alongside growth on renewal and expansion. The Customer Success Manager owns retention of the same portfolio, so together you make sure every account is both retained and growing.

Your customers include household names such as Adyen, BT, Sage, IKEA and Canva, and most are only scratching the surface of what Wordsmith can do. You will sit with their legal leaders, understand where AI can change how their teams work, and build the commercial case to roll Wordsmith out across their business. Few roles let you see so directly how your work drives a company's growth. You will partner closely with Customer Success, Sales, and Product and our founders.

 

What you'll do

Cross-sell and expand - Your number one priority: proactively grow your portfolio by cross-selling new products and use cases, adding seats and teams, and opening new parts of each customer's business, carrying and delivering against a growth quota.

Grow Revenue and Renewal - Own the growth on every renewal in your portfolio, building the commercial case for uplift and leading the pricing conversation, while the Customer Success Manager owns retention of the account.

Own the Commercial relationship - Be the trusted commercial point of contact for your customers, building relationships with both day-to-day users and economic buyers, and understanding each account's goals, risks, and opportunities.

Forecast with accuracy - Keep your pipeline and renewal forecast current and honest, take personal accountability for your forecast calls, confidence levels, and risk assessments, and explain what changes and why.

Run your patch like a business - Build and own account plans that map every buying centre, decision-maker and use case, then turn strong adoption into multi-year, multi-team commitments.

Partner across teams - Work symbiotically with the Customer Success Manager who owns retention of your portfolio: they keep accounts healthy and renewing, you drive growth on renewal, cross-sell and expansion. Partner with Sales on handover and with Product on what customers need next.

Be the voice of the customer - Feed what you hear back to the product and commercial teams so we build and sell the right things.

What success looks like

In your first 90 days: you know every account in your portfolio, have met the legal leaders and economic buyers, built an account plan for each, and closed your first expansion.

In your first 12 months: you have beaten your growth quota, landed at least one major cross-sell that opened a new part of a customer's business, and your forecast is one the leadership team relies on.

What we're looking for

Experience - At least 3 years of enterprise selling, with a consistent record of beating quota and growing enterprise accounts repeatedly and across multiple accounts. You are comfortable selling to the C-suite and General Counsel, and you have led complex, multi-stakeholder deals through procurement and security review.

Commercially Minded - You understand how to grow an account, you are comfortable talking price and value, and you connect daily customer work to retention and expansion outcomes.

Hands on with customers - Earn trust by being genuinely useful: you get on the call, write the business case, and chase the answer. Customers bring you their problems because you solve them.

Strong bias for action - You create opportunities rather than wait for them. When you see a gap in an account, you have a plan to close it by the end of the week.

A clear communicator - Comfortable writing and speaking with customers daily, and you can make technical things feel simple.

An exceptional operator - You run a disciplined pipeline, call your number accurately, and never let a follow-up slip, however busy the quarter gets.

Curious about Legal Tech - You do not need a legal background, but you are excited to learn the product deeply and become a genuine expert in it.

 

Why Wordsmith

  • Ground-floor seat at a fast-growing AI company, with a front-row view of how modern legal teams adopt AI.

  • A quota-carrying role where you own the proactive growth of your portfolio: cross-sell, expansion and growth on renewal.

  • Direct access to customers and to the founding team; your feedback shapes the product.

  • A team that ships fast, cares about customers, and will invest in your growth.

  • Real room to grow: as the Account Management team scales, so do the scope and leadership opportunities for the people who build it.

  • Work the way the future works: you will use AI agents every day to prepare, research and follow up, so more of your time goes on customers.

raw.description:
Sales Manager - Mid Market

London

 

Wordsmith

Legal touches everything that matters in a business: every deal, every hire, every launch, every risk. Sales runs on Salesforce. Engineering runs on GitHub. In-house legal runs on inboxes, chat threads and tools that weren’t built for it.
Wordsmith is changing that. We’re building the platform in-house legal runs on.

Requests from across the business come in through one front door. AI agents handle the routine work. Lawyers stay in control where judgment matters. Legal finally gets to triage by risk, not by whoever shouted loudest.

We’re built for in-house teams, not law firms. Our customers want to spend less on outside counsel, not more, and we’re on their side of that equation.

More than 500 companies run on Wordsmith, including Financial Times, Canva, Trip.com, Revolut, Adyen, Trustpilot, and Sage. We’ve raised $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, and we’re growing fast.

 

The Role

We're hiring a Sales Manager to lead and scale our Mid-Market UK&I team.

You'll own the number for your team, coach a group of full-cycle Account Executives, and build the processes that help them succeed. Your focus will be hiring, developing people, and driving consistent team performance.

This is an early-stage environment. Things move fast, priorities shift, and there isn't always a clear playbook. You'll need to make decisions, set the standard, and keep your team focused and moving.

 

What you'll do

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Mid-Market Account Executives

  • Own and consistently hit team revenue and pipeline targets

  • Run tight forecasting, pipeline reviews, and deal inspection

  • Raise the bar on discovery, demos, and value-led selling across the team

  • Hire, onboard, and ramp new Account Executives as we scale

  • Coach the team on building relationships with Legal Ops leaders, General Counsel, and Heads of Legal

  • Work closely with Product and Marketing to sharpen messaging and improve conversion

  • Keep pipeline clean and forecasts accurate; your CRM is your operating system

 

What we're looking for

  • SaaS sales experience, including time in mid-market

  • Experience managing and coaching a quota-carrying sales team

  • Track record of hitting and exceeding team targets

  • Strong in discovery, demo, and value-led selling, and able to teach it

  • Comfortable selling into complex organisations and senior stakeholders

  • High ownership; you take responsibility for outcomes, not just activity

  • Organised, consistent, and reliable with strong follow-through

 

How we work

We're an in-office team. We work together because it makes us faster, sharper, and more effective. You should expect to be in the office as your default.

This is a high performance environment. We set a high bar, move quickly, and expect people to take ownership of real problems.

There isn't always a clear path. The people who do well here figure things out, stay close to the work, and keep pushing until they get to the right outcome.

This won't suit everyone. If you're looking for a highly structured environment or clear boundaries around pace, this likely isn't the right fit.

Why Wordsmith

We're in a period of strong momentum, growing quickly, winning new customers, and expanding into larger accounts.

The product is landing well, the market is ready, and the team is scaling to meet demand.

If you want to build a team, develop great salespeople, and grow quickly in a high bar environment, this is one of the best places to do it.
